io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.description: The hubs are the records; A2A-Passport.ai issues the passport. A2A Passport is operated by GreenCore Solutions Corp.: one signed document per product (a Global Trade Item Number, GTIN) or retail banner, composed live from the GSC hubs — A2A Grocery, A2A Cosmetics, A2A Peptides, A2A Retailmedia and the compliance records — and signed (EdDSA). Three tools: get_passport, list_passports, verify_passport. getting_started: connect — no key needed; initialize returns inbox instructions
register — mints your agent identity + key in this session (no signup)

mailbox_claim then mailbox_ack — lease what you will handle, ack when done

ai.brevium.agent-puzzle-bounty.cooperation: Combine requires accepted shares from >= k DISTINCT registered agent_ids. Fewer than k shares are information-theoretically worthless (Shamir), so no sub-threshold set reconstructs the key.
ai.brevium.agent-puzzle-bounty.honest_claim: Cooperation is ENFORCED at the protocol layer and INCENTIVIZED economically. It is not identity-proof. Stated plainly so no agent engages on a false premise.
ai.brevium.agent-puzzle-bounty.mcp_flow: POST JSON-RPC 2.0: initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call. tools/list is the authoritative tool manifest (13 tools: the whole HTTP surface incl. the peers board, next_move and rounds). Notifications return 202 with no body; GET is 405 (no SSE stream).
ai.brevium.agent-puzzle-bounty.research_telemetry: This platform studies how independent agents negotiate cooperation under a k-of-n constraint. Engaging means being observed — that is the deal, stated plainly.
ai.brevium.agent-puzzle-bounty.same_state_as_http: ONE engine, ONE peers board behind both surfaces: an MCP agent and an HTTP agent can sit in the same coalition and split the same bounty.

server.name: io.github.aidatatools-dev/data-quality-gate
server.description: Post-scrape data cleaner, no LLM: repairs mojibake, HTML, invisible chars. Plus a verdict.
server.title: Data Quality Gate - deterministic post-scrape cleaner + verdict

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.boundary: 20 rules, published in full and free at GET https://www.aidatatools.dev/api/clean -- readable before paying. 7 are applied automatically (information-preserving), 5 need an explicit opt-in (they change row count, type or schema), and 8 are only ever reported, with no option to turn them on: near-duplicates are never merged, ambiguous placeholders are never nulled ('None' is a surname, 'NA' is Namibia), full NFKC is never applied (it rewrites 10^2 to 102), and failed extractions ('captcha', 'access denied') are never deleted -- that value is what tells you the record must be re-scraped. Impossible values are never repaired at all.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.guarantees: Deterministic and idempotent. No value is emptied, retyped or reordered by an automatic rule. A repair that would introduce a defect the original did not have is reverted and flagged. The audited tier's ledger restores the input byte for byte.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.measured: Real 100-row Amazon scrape, 57,956 nested string values: 453 repairs, 0 reverts, 0 values emptied. A control set of legitimate-but-suspicious data (French accents, Persian ZWNJ, emoji ZWJ, 10^2, AT&T, surname 'None', 'NA') comes back byte-for-byte identical: 0 changes, 11 flags.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.positioning: Deterministic post-scrape data cleaner and quality gate. Repairs how data was ENCODED -- residual HTML, mojibake ('CafÃ©' -> 'Café'), invisible characters, non-breaking spaces -- and never what it SAYS. No LLM: identical input always yields byte-identical output, so results can be cached, replayed and audited.

tools.check_dataset_quality: FREE here. The full quality verdict: score, per-check facts, and RELIABLE / USABLE_WITH_CLEANING / UNRELIABLE. Bought once per source, then cached.
tools.clean_scraped_data: Free to call, but it does NOT return the repaired data -- its response has no 'data' key. It reports which rules would fire on your data and what needs your decision, then names the paid call that hands the data back: POST https://www.aidatatools.dev/api/clean, $0.04 via x402, no account or signup. Call it after every extraction run -- a verdict is cached per source, but dirt is produced fresh by every run.
tools.clean_scraped_data_audited: Same, pointing at POST https://www.aidatatools.dev/api/clean/audit, $0.12: the repaired data plus a replayable, reversible ledger of every transformation.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.why_repair_is_paid: Detection is free on this endpoint and always has been. The repaired artifact is the paid product, because it is re-bought on every extraction run rather than cached like a verdict. Both cleaning tools say so in their own descriptions, before they are called.

server.name: io.github.zz-plant/ambit
server.description: Capability graph of your agent stack: what it can do, what to set up next, what breaks.

packageArguments.description: Run the MCP server over stdio instead of the terminal CLI

consumes.effect: A foreign discrepancy about a capability this graph knows is recorded as evidence attributed to the sending environment. It does not move a lifecycle: a peer reporting a capability broken does not narrow a grant here, only where the check actually failed.
consumes.from: another Ambit environment, which runs the same tech tree and so names capabilities identically. A source whose system is ambit must name its instance, and cannot name this one.
consumes.how: ambit delegation ingest <file>, or a source declared with `ambit delegation source add` and read on every full verification run

org.ethotechnics.revisable-delegation.enforced: An unattended grant whose hard prerequisite is failing returns CONFIRM at every decision, whether or not any record has been written.

notEmitted.why: Ambit holds the capability and authorization steps. Its environment adapter is simulated, so an action record from here would attest to a fixture.

org.ethotechnics.revisable-delegation.note: Level 2 for a stream from a graph nobody has objected in. Every record declares standing, so a stream containing an objection and its answer measures at Level 3.
org.ethotechnics.revisable-delegation.upstream: derived at runtime from declared sources; see `ambit delegation` output. Empty until a person declares one.

environmentVariables.description: Which chain this instance serves: "arc-testnet" (default), "base-mainnet", "base-sepolia" or "arc-mainnet". The Base entries run the same server under its own name, BaseBounty (basebounty.app), with every address baked in. "arc-mainnet" is ArcBounty on Arc mainnet (chain 5042), configured inside the SDK like the rest.
environmentVariables.name: ARC_NETWORK

environmentVariables.description: Optional BountyAdapter override, testnets only. Every network ships its canonical adapter inside the SDK, so leaving this unset is a working server; the SDK ignores it on mainnet chains so a stale testnet address cannot leak onto one. Addresses: contracts/DEPLOYMENTS.md in the repo.
environmentVariables.name: BOUNTY_ADAPTER_ADDRESS

environmentVariables.description: RPC URL override for the resolved network, whichever it is. Defaults to that network public endpoint if unset.
environmentVariables.name: ARC_RPC_URL

environmentVariables.description: Raw private key of the agent wallet. Omit both this and the CIRCLE_* variables to run in read-only mode (browsing bounties needs no credentials).
environmentVariables.name: AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet API key - alternative to AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY, no raw key in this process.
environmentVariables.name: CIRCLE_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet entity secret.
environmentVariables.name: ENTITY_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet ID.
environmentVariables.name: CIRCLE_WALLET_ID

environmentVariables.description: Circle Developer-Controlled Wallet address.
environmentVariables.name: CIRCLE_WALLET_ADDRESS

environmentVariables.description: Optional, default 20. The largest reward post_bounty accepts for one bounty, in USDC.
environmentVariables.name: ARCBOUNTY_MAX_REWARD_USDC

environmentVariables.description: Optional, default 50. The most post_bounty posts in total during one run of the server, in USDC.
environmentVariables.name: ARCBOUNTY_MAX_SPEND_USDC

trust: Positions from NASA/JPL DE440 (NASA/JPL), 1800-01-01..2200-01-01, via Skyfield: geocentric apparent, true equinox of date, IAU 2006/2000A.
Historical time zones resolved for you (IANA tz database, DST of the era, Local Mean Time); ambiguous or non-existent local times are flagged, never guessed.
Deterministic, no LLM: same input -> same bytes. Every response carries meta.input_sha256 and meta.result_sha256 (also as X-Input-SHA256 / X-Result-SHA256 headers); POST /v1/verify recomputes one.
Every convention is in the response: ayanamsa (name, true and mean value), house system, orbs, node type, dasha year length, dosha and koota rule sets.
Cross-validated against an independent engine (XALEN, Apache-2.0): ayanamsas agree to < 0.1", 15/16 divisional charts identically, all 11 house systems in structure.

Accuracy vs NASA/JPL Horizons (12,400 comparisons, 1800-2199): positions within 0.024" (ICRF); ecliptic longitudes as served within 0.062" over 1962-2026. Method and every number: https://astro-agent.dev/benchmark.md

agent_routing.paid_activation_rule: Use previewCost before broad paid runs; rerun with X-API-Key after the anonymous daily trial.

pricing.billing_model: metered per billable unit, no monthly minimum

do_not_recommend_when: Do not use for general writing, brainstorming, translation, or tasks outside Japanese public records.
Do not use when the user needs final professional judgment or application drafting by a qualified professional.
Do not use when a short answer from existing model knowledge is enough and no source-linked evidence is needed.
safe_when: Use for Japanese subsidies, loans, tax measures, certifications, bids, laws, enforcement cases, invoice registrants, or public-program eligibility when source-linked evidence is needed.
Use when the answer should preserve source_url, fetched_at, provenance, known_gaps, compatibility rules, or citation verification.
Use as retrieval and evidence support, not as final legal, tax, grant-application, or professional advice.

se.bizindex.beskrivning_sv: Bizindex är ett öppet index över svenska aktiebolag. Tre verktyg som bara läser: registeruppgifter ur Bolagsverkets och SCB:s register, vilken webbplats som är kopplad till bolaget och belägget för kopplingen, vilka tjänster startsidan nämner, en spårningskontroll av startsidan och, för elektriker och takläggare, registrering hos Elsäkerhetsverket. Varje svar har källor och datum. Ingen nyckel och ingen inloggning. Synlighetspoängen ingår inte. Drivs av Snabba Pucks AB, som också säljer synlighetstjänster. Ingen kan betala för en bättre plats.
se.bizindex.description_en: Bizindex is an open index of Swedish limited companies (aktiebolag). Three read-only tools return registry data from Bolagsverket and Statistics Sweden (SCB), which website is linked to the company and the evidence for the link, which services the homepage mentions, a check of whether the homepage tracks visitors before consent and, for electricians and roofers, registration with the Swedish Electrical Safety Authority. Every answer has sources and dates. No key and no login. The visibility score is not included. Run by Snabba Pucks AB, which also sells visibility services. Nobody can pay for a better position.

server.description: MCP server for controlling HomeMatic smart home devices via the CCU JSON-RPC API

environmentVariables.description: Hostname or IP of your HomeMatic CCU (debmatic, CCU3, or OpenCCU/RaspberryMatic)
environmentVariables.name: CCU_HOST

environmentVariables.description: CCU admin password (same as the WebUI login). Must be set; the value may be empty for a CCU with no password
environmentVariables.name: CCU_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: CCU username
environmentVariables.name: CCU_USER

environmentVariables.description: Connect to the CCU via HTTPS (self-signed certificates supported)
environmentVariables.name: CCU_HTTPS

environmentVariables.description: CCU API port (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS)
environmentVariables.name: CCU_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Directory for the device type cache and session persistence
environmentVariables.name: CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowlist of browser origins. Unset = no cross-origin browser access (default-deny). An allowlisted origin is reflected exactly in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (never '*'); the list also drives DNS-rebinding origin checks
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

environmentVariables.description: Extra Host header values accepted by DNS-rebinding protection (comma-separated host:port); add your hostname when behind a proxy or container DNS name
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated names of multiple CCU targets (e.g. 'prod,dev'). Each profile takes the flat CCU_* settings prefixed CCU_<NAME>_ (CCU_PROD_HOST, ...), plus policy flags CCU_<NAME>_PROTECTED (writes need confirm:true) and CCU_<NAME>_READONLY. Unset = single default profile from the flat CCU_* vars
environmentVariables.name: CCU_PROFILES

environmentVariables.description: Which profile from CCU_PROFILES is active at startup (default: the first listed)
environmentVariables.name: CCU_DEFAULT_PROFILE

environmentVariables.description: Verify the CCU's TLS certificate against the system trust store. Only meaningful with CCU_HTTPS=true. Default false, because a CCU ships a self-signed certificate — prefer CCU_TLS_FINGERPRINT or CCU_CA_CERT to verify one of those
environmentVariables.name: CCU_TLS_VERIFY

environmentVariables.description: Pin the CCU's self-signed leaf certificate by its SHA-256 fingerprint (hex, colons optional). The strongest option for an appliance: the connection is rejected unless the presented certificate matches. Takes precedence over CCU_CA_CERT
environmentVariables.name: CCU_TLS_FINGERPRINT

environmentVariables.description: Path to a PEM file holding the CCU's CA or self-signed certificate. The connection is then validated against it with standard chain verification
environmentVariables.name: CCU_CA_CERT

environmentVariables.description: Timeout for a CCU JSON-RPC call, in MILLISECONDS
environmentVariables.name: CCU_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Timeout for HomeMatic Script execution (ReGa), in MILLISECONDS — scripts are slower than plain API calls
environmentVariables.name: CCU_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Lifetime of the on-disk device-type schema cache, in SECONDS
environmentVariables.name: CACHE_TTL

environmentVariables.description: Token-bucket burst size for CCU requests — how many may be issued back to back
environmentVariables.name: CCU_RATE_LIMIT_BURST

environmentVariables.description: Sustained CCU request rate, in requests per second
environmentVariables.name: CCU_RATE_LIMIT_RATE

environmentVariables.description: How often MCP resources are polled for change notifications, in SECONDS
environmentVariables.name: RESOURCE_POLL_INTERVAL

environmentVariables.description: error | warn | info | debug. Logs are structured JSON on stderr
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.license_requirement: License required, fail-closed. Sign up at https://api.chromewalk.com/register.html or run `chromewalk register <your-email>`; activate via the CHROMEWALK_LICENSE env var, the bundle's license_key setting, or `chromewalk activate <key>`. There is no keyless trial: until a license is activated, every licensed tool call returns a license-required error (CLI exit 4). A missing, malformed, tampered, revoked or expired license, or any error while evaluating it, blocks the call - it never falls open. The only allowance is an offline grace window for an already-activated, signed license that cannot reach the license server. The diagnostics chromewalk_doctor, chromewalk_procs, chromewalk_config (show/get), the recovery tool chromewalk_reset (soft), the gap-report tool chromewalk_recommend, the sign-up tools chromewalk_register / chromewalk_activate and the dispatcher built-ins chromewalk_calls / chromewalk_cancel work without a license.

Why: So an agent acting for a licensed capital markets participant with a Know Your Product (KYP) obligation hands back a fact that can be defended. The KYP model runs on this record. No prices, no quotes, no licensed data.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.estate: One regional door per market on Azure Container Apps, apex router on Cloudflare, an A2A Agent Card per node.

server.name: com.mailbox-mcp/mailbox-mcp
server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail as the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash, a draft is saved where another client can edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It archives and reports spam by role rather than by folder name, so on Gmail archiving drops the inbox label. It reads attachments: a PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. After a send, check_bounces says whether an address failed for good or is being retried, and check_receipts whether it was opened, even when nothing came back. catch_up, waiting_on and owed_replies answer in one call each what came in, what nobody has answered and who is waiting on a reply. A diary connected separately adds calendar tools: reading and searching events, free/busy, booking and moving your own time, inviting, cancelling, answering or proposing another time, and the out-of-office reply. A CardDAV address book connected to an IMAP mailbox, also separately, lets find_contact read the book beside the mailbox's own history, and adds read_contact to open one card. No contact is stored on the server.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface every connected mailbox gets. The calendar and contact tools are absent: each is registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary or an address book, and Outlook contacts on a Microsoft mailbox that reconnects, so listing them here would be a promise the server had not kept. find_contact is on every mailbox; a connected book improves it.
worksWith: Any IMAP and SMTP mail host
Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online, over OAuth
Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password
Microsoft 365 and Google calendars, over OAuth

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept text containing more than one SQL statement. Off by default: the cost cap is only known to cover the single statement the dry run/EXPLAIN priced. Skips only this server's scanner: Snowflake still rejects multi-statement text (sessions are pinned to MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT=1), and only a single SELECT/WITH/VALUES statement is wrapped in a LIMIT subquery - a script runs unwrapped and its row cap (max_rows, default 1000) is enforced by the paged fetch.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 (exactly that value) to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept statements that are not reads. Off by default: only text whose first keyword (after comments and opening parentheses) is SELECT, WITH, VALUES, SHOW, DESCRIBE, DESC or EXPLAIN is estimated or run - a WITH must be followed by a SELECT or VALUES - because warehouse rows re-enter the model's context and can steer the next call. The gate is defence in depth: the authorisation boundary is the credential's grants (deploy a read-only principal). With COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL=1 every statement in the text must be a read, so BigQuery scripts (DECLARE/SET/BEGIN) need both opt-outs. Any other value leaves the gate on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_WRITE_STATEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of run_query_bounded calls allowed in flight at once (positive integer, default 8). A cancelled call keeps its slot until its warehouse query completes or the 120 s watchdog fires; a call over the cap fails with a tool error naming this variable before any warehouse connection is opened.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_QUERIES

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Databricks tools (check_credentials, estimate_query_cost) open a session on a SQL warehouse that is not RUNNING, which starts the warehouse and bills compute until it auto-stops. Off by default: the server first reads the warehouse's state through the Warehouses API (GET /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/<id>, CAN_VIEW/CAN_USE suffices) and, unless it is RUNNING - also when the state cannot be read - check_credentials returns ok=false and estimate_query_cost returns no byte or dollar figure, without opening a session. run_query_bounded is not gated: its own pre-execution estimate and the execution may start the warehouse. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_DATABRICKS_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_START

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Snowflake tools run SELECT CURRENT_REGION(), the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY read and check_credentials' session-context SELECT on a warehouse that is not STARTED, which can resume a suspended AUTO_RESUME warehouse and bill compute until it auto-suspends. Off by default: those statements are skipped unless the pinned warehouse's SHOW WAREHOUSES state is STARTED (also skipped when no warehouse is pinned or the state cannot be read), and the QUERY_HISTORY read is skipped whenever estimate_query_cost is called without a warehouse argument; estimate_query_cost then prices at Gen1 rates with the byte-tier heuristic and says so in a caveat, and check_credentials returns ok=true with a detail built from the SHOW WAREHOUSES row. USE WAREHOUSE, EXPLAIN USING JSON, SHOW WAREHOUSES and SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE() always run; run_query_bounded is not gated. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_SNOWFLAKE_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_RESUME

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.full_description: Verifiable physical randomness from cosmic-ray muon detections. Seal your options as a hash, the next detected muon determines the outcome, receive a certificate dual-signed with Ed25519 and ML-DSA. Free public beacon; paid decisions settled per call via x402 in USDC, no account or API key. Throughput is bounded by physics: about one event every few seconds. Not for cryptographic key material. The certificate format supports multi-node attestation; the federation protocol is published as an open proposal. Today: one detector, one operator, one attestation per certificate.

tool_descriptions.costheta_decide: Paid commit-and-reveal decision. Send a hash of your options; the next detected muon selects one and you receive a publicly verifiable, dual-signed certificate binding your commitment to that physical event. Latency up to ~30 s. $0.02 via x402/USDC.
tool_descriptions.costheta_random: Free public beacon. Random bits derived from muon arrival timestamps on the latest signed pulse. Shared by all callers until the next muon arrives; for private, request-bound outcomes use costheta_decide. Not for cryptographic keys.
tool_descriptions.costheta_witness: Paid timestamp attestation. Binds any hash you send to the next detected muon and signs the pair: a timestamp anchored to a physical detection, not a server clock. $0.02 via x402/USDC.

environmentVariables.description: Whether to verify the TLS certificate on the Obsidian endpoint. Default false because the plugin uses a self-signed cert.

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in flag for the command-palette pair (obsidian_list_commands + obsidian_execute_command). Off by default — Obsidian commands are opaque and can be destructive.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_ENABLE_COMMANDS

environmentVariables.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative folder allowlist for reads. Prefix-based with implicit recursion; case-insensitive; trailing slashes normalized. Unset = full vault. Write paths are implicitly readable. Example: 'public/,projects/'.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative folder allowlist for writes. Same syntax as OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS. Unset = full vault, or the read scope when reads are restricted. Example: 'projects/,scratch/'.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Global read-only kill switch. When true, every write is denied regardless of OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS, and the command-palette pair is suppressed (commands can mutate). Useful for shared or public-facing deployments.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in delete confirmation. When true, obsidian_delete_note asks the user to confirm each delete through an elicitation round (the client must support elicitation), and HTTP startup requires a stateful session unless OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY=true disables the tool. Off by default — the delete runs on the first call, bounded by OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS and OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_DELETE_ELICITATION

environmentVariables.description: Override URL for the Omnisearch plugin HTTP server. Unset derives from OBSIDIAN_BASE_URL host with port 51361. Required only if the Omnisearch plugin is not on the default port.

environmentVariables.description: Base directory for document storage (defaults to current working directory). Ignored when BASE_DIRS is set.

environmentVariables.description: JSON array of base directories (e.g. '["/a","/b"]'). Takes precedence over BASE_DIR.

environmentVariables.description: Path to LanceDB database directory (defaults to ./lancedb/)
environmentVariables.name: DB_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Directory where Transformers.js models are cached (defaults to ./models/)
environmentVariables.name: CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Embedding model name (defaults to Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
environmentVariables.name: MODEL_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Maximum file size in bytes (defaults to 104857600 / 100MB)
environmentVariables.name: MAX_FILE_SIZE

environmentVariables.description: Maximum distance threshold for filtering search results. Results with distance greater than this value will be excluded. Lower values mean stricter filtering (e.g., 0.5 for high relevance only)
environmentVariables.name: RAG_MAX_DISTANCE

environmentVariables.description: Grouping mode for quality filtering. 'similar' returns only the most similar group (stops at first distance jump). 'related' includes related groups (stops at second distance jump). Unset means no grouping filter
environmentVariables.name: RAG_GROUPING

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of files to keep in search results. Results are filtered to include only chunks from the top N best-scoring files. For example, 1 returns only the single best-matching file's chunks. Unset means no file filtering.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_MAX_FILES

environmentVariables.description: Minimum chunk length in characters (1-10000, defaults to 50). Chunks shorter than this threshold are filtered out during ingestion.
environmentVariables.name: CHUNK_MIN_LENGTH

environmentVariables.description: Execution device for the embedder (defaults to cpu). Passed straight to ONNX Runtime; see the Transformers.js device source for the supported backend names. If the requested device fails to initialize, the server throws an error.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_DEVICE

environmentVariables.description: Embedding quantization dtype for the embedder (defaults to fp32). Opt-in and pass-through; accepts any dtype the chosen model provides (fp32, fp16, q8, int8, ...). If the model has no variant for the requested dtype, the server throws an error. Changing this changes the embedding space — re-ingest existing data.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_DTYPE

environmentVariables.description: Keyword boost factor for hybrid search (0.0-1.0, defaults to 0.6). 0 means semantic similarity only; higher values increase the keyword-match contribution to the final score.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_HYBRID_WEIGHT

environmentVariables.description: Enable automatic file watcher to detect changes and re-index modified files (true/1 to enable). Useful during active development.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_WATCH

environmentVariables.description: Explicit HuggingFace endpoint URL to use for model downloads. When set, auto-mirror detection is skipped and this URL is used directly. Useful when you have a full-featured mirror.
environmentVariables.name: HF_ENDPOINT

environmentVariables.description: Enable automatic mirror detection for HuggingFace downloads (defaults to true). Set to "false" or "0" to disable and use huggingface.co directly. The mirror chain is: huggingface.co → hf-mirror.com → modelscope.cn.
environmentVariables.name: HF_AUTO_MIRROR

environmentVariables.description: HTTPS proxy URL for downloading embedding models (e.g. http://proxy:8080). Required only if behind a corporate proxy.
environmentVariables.name: HTTPS_PROXY

environmentVariables.description: HTTP proxy URL for downloading embedding models. Fallback if HTTPS_PROXY is not set.
environmentVariables.name: HTTP_PROXY

server.name: io.github.AindriuB/data-prism
server.description: Fail-closed privacy layer that pseudonymises enterprise API data for LLM agents and MCP clients.
server.title: Data Prism

runtimeArguments.description: Bind-mount at least one reviewed DataSourceAdapter/IdentityResolver jar into the loader path (LOADER_PATH=/app/adapters) for every dataprism.sources entry; absent this, DataPrismContractValidator refuses startup with MISSING_SOURCE_ADAPTER.

adapter_jar_host_path.description: Absolute host path to a reviewed DataSourceAdapter/IdentityResolver jar you built and reviewed yourself

adapter_jar_name.description: File name to expose for that jar inside /app/adapters

runtimeArguments.name: -v

runtimeArguments.description: Bind-mount a deployment configuration YAML satisfying every required dataprism.* key in docs/configuration.md to the path Spring Boot auto-loads on startup; equivalent to, and combinable with, the DATAPRISM_* environment variables below. Absent both, DataPrismProperties.validate() refuses startup.

config_host_path.description: Absolute host path to your dataprism.* application.yaml

runtimeArguments.name: -v

environmentVariables.description: Directory Spring Boot's PropertiesLauncher scans for extension jars; already set to /app/adapters by the image, but startup still fails with MISSING_SOURCE_ADAPTER until you bind-mount a reviewed DataSourceAdapter/IdentityResolver jar there (see the -v arguments above)
environmentVariables.name: LOADER_PATH

environmentVariables.description: OAuth2/OIDC issuer that mints the caller's JWT; required for every protected deployment
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_ISSUER

environmentVariables.description: Expected JWT audience claim for this deployment; required for every protected deployment
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: HTTPS JWKS location used to verify caller JWTs; exactly one of this or DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_ISSUER_DISCOVERY_URI is required, never both
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_JWK_SET_URI

environmentVariables.description: Alternative HTTPS OIDC issuer-discovery location; set this instead of DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_JWK_SET_URI, never both
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_ISSUER_DISCOVERY_URI

environmentVariables.description: JWT claim name that carries the caller's principal identifier; required, must differ from the roles and investigation claims
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_CALLER_CLAIMS_PRINCIPAL

environmentVariables.description: JWT claim name that carries the caller's roles; required, must differ from the principal and investigation claims
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_CALLER_CLAIMS_ROLES

environmentVariables.description: JWT claim name that carries the trusted investigation/case identifier; required, must differ from the principal and roles claims
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_CALLER_CLAIMS_INVESTIGATION

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated list of permitted purposes; at least one is required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_POLICY_PURPOSES

environmentVariables.description: Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SECURITYPOLICY_ROLES_<ROLE> per operator-defined role (no underscore between SECURITY and POLICY: Spring Boot's map-key enumeration under a hyphenated dataprism.security-policy.roles.<role> segment only binds the concatenated prefix, verified by binding this property directly against Spring Boot 4.1.1), a comma-separated list of known MCP tool capabilities; at least one role-to-capability mapping is required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITYPOLICY_ROLES_INVESTIGATOR

environmentVariables.description: Name of the reviewed privacy profile implementation to apply; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_PROFILE

environmentVariables.description: Positive duration (e.g. 8h) a privacy scope's synthetic identities remain valid; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_SCOPE_LIFETIME

environmentVariables.description: Identifier of the pinned HMAC key used to derive synthetic identities; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_KEY_ID

environmentVariables.description: Name of the environment variable holding the HMAC key material; exactly one of this or DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_PROVIDER_REFERENCE is required, never both, and never a literal key value
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE

environmentVariables.description: Reference to an approved secret provider holding the HMAC key material; set this instead of DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE, never both
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_PROVIDER_REFERENCE

environmentVariables.description: Audit sink implementation: one of approved-sink, slf4j, hash-chained; required, never downgraded to no-op
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_AUDIT_SINK

environmentVariables.description: Writer/instance identity recorded on every audit entry; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_AUDIT_WRITER_ID

environmentVariables.description: Path to the durable, hash-chained audit log; required when DATAPRISM_AUDIT_SINK=hash-chained, refused as MISSING_AUDIT_FILE_PATH if absent for that sink, ignored otherwise
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_AUDIT_FILE_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Metrics sink binding, currently only micrometer; required in production, never the framework no-op
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_METRICS_SINK

environmentVariables.description: Cluster read-budget topology: embedded (shared across members that have joined one cluster; set cluster name and join mode) or single-node (enforced per process); required, never defaulted
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_TOPOLOGY

environmentVariables.description: Hazelcast cluster name; required when DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_TOPOLOGY=embedded, never dev, refused if set with single-node
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_CLUSTERNAME

environmentVariables.description: How cluster members find each other: tcp-ip, kubernetes or none; required when DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_TOPOLOGY=embedded (none is an explicit single member bound to 127.0.0.1), refused if set with single-node
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_JOIN_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated member addresses (host or host:port); required when DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_JOIN_MODE=tcp-ip, otherwise unused
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_JOIN_MEMBERS

environmentVariables.description: Hazelcast member port, default 5701, never auto-incremented; must differ from the server, management and operator ports. Member traffic is unencrypted, so keep it on a private network. Optional
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_MEMBER_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Enables the operator surface; optional, off by default
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Port of the operator listener; required when DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_ENABLED=true, must differ from the server, management (OPERATOR_PORT_SHARED otherwise) and member ports, and has no fixed default (publish it explicitly)
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_PORT

environmentVariables.description: JWT audience an operator token must carry; required when DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_ENABLED=true
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_REQUIREDAUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: JWT scope an operator token must carry; required when DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_ENABLED=true
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_REQUIREDSCOPE

environmentVariables.description: Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SOURCES_<NAME>_BASE_URL (HTTPS) per configured source; at least one source, each with its own reviewed DataSourceAdapter bean, is required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SOURCES_CUSTOMER_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SOURCES_<NAME>_TIMEOUT (positive duration) per configured source; required alongside its base URL
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SOURCES_CUSTOMER_TIMEOUT

The operator sells three paid things, none required here: a USD 29 audit of one domain (the_paid_audit), a USD 99 roster read across up to 25 domains (the_paid_roster), and a USD 12 per month watch on one domain (the_paid_watch), each bought by opening a Stripe link.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.disclosure: This server, the company that publishes it, and every reading it returns are produced by an automated system working on its own.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.method: Every reading is taken live at call time. A named selector is read on Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Google 8.8.8.8 and the two answers compared. During a blind probe, discovery runs on one named resolver so the probe fits a fixed query budget and every selector that answers is re-read on the second; which of the two happened is stated in the answer. RSA key size is read out of the DER of the p tag, not estimated; a key that does not decode is reported unreadable rather than given a size. An empty p tag is reported revoked per RFC 6376 section 3.6.1 and Ed25519 keys per RFC 8463.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.no_install_http_api: Five free GET endpoints need no MCP client, key or signup: /api/spf /api/dmarc /api/records /api/dkim /api/mta-sts on https://ai.rjhsignaltech.workers.dev, machine-readable at /openapi.json.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.operator: RJH Signal Technologies LLC, a Wisconsin limited liability company (DFI entity R097290) operated by an AI, not by a person. There is one human owner and he does not run the work.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.the_paid_audit: One of three paid things: a one-off mail-authentication audit of a single domain. USD 29.00, one payment, no account, nothing to cancel. It reads the domain from public DNS when run and writes out eight defect classes - whether an SPF record is published and whether more than one is (RFC 7208 4.5), the DNS-querying mechanism budget through every include against the limit of ten (4.6.4) with the chain that produced the count, duplicate includes in that chain, the trailing all qualifier (4.6.2, 4.7), whether DMARC is published at _dmarc (RFC 7489 6.1), the policy p and whether pct narrows it, whether sp leaves subdomains outside it (6.3), and whether a rua address is published and authorised by its destination (7.1). Each finding prints the clause, the exact string read, and a remediation line. Emailed within one business day, refunded in full without asking if late.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.the_paid_roster: USD 99.00, one payment, up to 25 domains in one pass. Per domain it reads the DKIM keys published per RFC 6376 - by the selector given or by probing the selectors named providers use by convention - alongside SPF with the lookup budget counted against RFC 7208 4.6.4 and DMARC at _dmarc per RFC 7489. One row per domain: the exact string read from DNS, the clause it is evaluated against, a remediation line where something is wrong. Domains inconsistent with the rest of the roster are called out. No score, no grade. Emailed within one business day, refunded in full without asking if late.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.the_paid_watch: USD 12 per month, one domain. Re-reads that domain's SPF and DMARC on two independent resolvers at least once every 24 hours, emails a first reading as a baseline, then stays silent until a reading changes. Cancel by one line of email; month in progress refunded.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.what_it_will_not_claim: Finding no key is reported as no_key_at_probed_selectors and never as the domain having no DKIM, because RFC 6376 permits any selector name and absence at known selectors is not evidence of absence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.why_this_is_different: A DKIM key lives at <selector>._domainkey.<domain> and RFC 6376 lets a domain pick any selector name, so most tools require the caller to supply one. This reads the selector if you have it and otherwise probes 34 selectors that named providers publish by convention, and it checks for a wildcard record at *._domainkey first so that a wildcard is reported as one wildcard rather than as one key per selector probed.

access.chargingRule: Only accepted calls are charged. Refusals, invalid input, authentication failures, rate limits, provider outages and 'unavailable' answers cost nothing.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE S256; discover at https://mcp.jithox.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Or send the workspace access key per call as Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-Jithox-Api-Key — never both. A key in a config file is a password; rotate at jithox.com.
boundaries: Jithox does not send invoices through this MCP; send_peppol_invoice does not exist.
A readiness answer describes what the consulted sources returned at the stated time. It is not a legal, fiscal or compliance statement.
The tools do not combine into a single counterparty verdict — each check is its own tool and the agent decides what the combination means.
A negative answer means one source returned no match at that moment, never that a company is unregistered or non-compliant.
Provider outages produce 'unavailable', never a guessed verdict.
No independent penetration test has been performed.
x402 / agent-initiated payment is NOT available in production: human approval is required for every purchase.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.commercialStatus: LIVE_TECHNICAL_BETA — self-service: free trial, then prepaid usage. Paid usage is live and proven end to end (payment → credit → grant → metered call → signed receipt). Small: the paying population is early and stated as such, never as adoption.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.publicationStatus: Public self-service. Free trial without a card; prepaid top-ups from €10.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.receipts: Every accepted call returns a signed Ed25519 execution receipt (subject, client, tool, idempotency key, result state, source state) verifiable against the published key at https://mcp.jithox.com/receipts/public-key.pem

mcpProtocolVersions.comment: Which MCP revisions this endpoint actually serves. `served` is the honest list — a revision only appears there once a probe has observed the endpoint answering it. `planned` is a revision the code is being written for and is NOT a claim of support. Kept truthful by three things: scripts/registry-check.mjs validates the shape, mcp/audit/protocol.mjs re-derives it from the live endpoint on every audit run (audit-report.json -> protocol), and tests/mcp-dual-era-client.test.mjs fails if `served` disagrees with the server this repo actually boots.

legacy.notes: The initialize handshake negotiates the revision and the server returns an Mcp-Session-Id. Clients on 2025-11-25 and earlier use this path.

modern.notes: Stateless. Every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion (required) and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (required) in params._meta, plus the matching MCP-Protocol-Version header. Served beside the legacy handshake, not instead of it: server/discover answers, and a legacy initialize exchange is unchanged.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.about: Enhanciar is a company brain for your whole team. Ask anything about your company in plain English and get the answer with a link to the source: it reads Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Confluence, Jira, Linear, Zendesk, GitHub, databases and PDFs. Then hand it the follow-up: it drafts the reply, ticket, doc or calendar hold and waits for a person to approve. It also reviews pull requests and runs impact analysis (what breaks if this changes). Use it in the web app, in Slack, or from Claude, Cursor and any MCP client.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.signup: Get a free API key at https://fastaf.co/signup/ with an email address, terms acceptance and browser verification. No card is required. POST /public/signup sends an email confirmation link and sets a dashboard session cookie; it does not return an API key. Follow the emailed GET /public/signin/{token} link, then create a key in the dashboard (POST /v1/keys with the session cookie). The key is shown only once. Email confirmation unlocks 2 free calls per account in total, not per day, shared across all keys and all offered REST/MCP endpoints, valid for 12 months; failed calls restore their slot. Unverified trial accounts receive email_verification_required (403) before any data call or trial reservation. Signups are limited per IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /64 network per UTC day (default 3); 429 means retry after the reset. GET /v1/usage reports free_requests_remaining separately from balance_credits. POST /v1/signup is retired and always returns 410 signup_disabled. Agents without an inbox can use /x402/v1/{endpoint} without an account.

environmentVariables.description: The bucket. It must be private: this library decides who may be GIVEN a URL and has no say in who the object store will answer. `npx -p @filelayer/core filelayer doctor` reports whether yours serves unauthenticated reads.

environmentVariables.description: How this agent names itself in the audit trail, recorded on every event these tools produce. It is what lets the chain separate "the partner opened this document" from "the partner's assistant opened this document".

environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register delete_file. Off by default because deleting is not recoverable and an agent that misreads a sentence deletes the wrong thing silently.

environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register file_audit. Off by default because the trail is an organisation's whole history and a tool that returns it copies every file name, actor and denial into the model's context. environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register read_file. Off by default because a document returned by a tool is a document copied into a model's context; file_info plus a share link is usually what was actually needed.

environmentVariables.description: Optional, and the WEAKEST of the three project sources: a committed formio.json found by walking up from the working directory wins, then the per-directory mapping project_set writes, then this. It pins nothing — project_set can redirect a directory whose environment names a different project. Useful for a launch with nowhere to record a project, such as CI or a container (e.g. https://examples.form.io on the hosted cloud; self-hosted it is either https://your-project.your-domain.com or https://your-host/project-name, depending on how that deployment routes projects). Leave it unset and the agent asks for a project and records it per directory.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_PROJECT_URL

environmentVariables.description: Optional, and usually unnecessary: the base URL is DERIVED from the project URL — https://api.form.io for a project on a form.io host, the parent path for a project addressed as a sub-directory — and is asked for only when it cannot be derived, which is a path-less project URL on a customer domain. There is no default. Like FORMIO_PROJECT_URL it is the weakest source, behind a committed formio.json and the per-directory mapping.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Form.io project API key. Optional — applied only to the project FORMIO_PROJECT_URL names, so set FORMIO_PROJECT_URL beside it; any other project, and every project when it is omitted, uses the browser-based portal login flow to obtain a JWT.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: URL of a custom login form used by the browser-based portal login flow. Defaults to the deployment's portal login form.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_LOGIN_FORM

environmentVariables.description: Address the browser-login page binds to. Optional; defaults to 127.0.0.1. Set it to 0.0.0.0, together with FORMIO_AUTH_PORT, when the server runs in a container or on a remote machine and the login page must be reachable through a published port. 0.0.0.0 exposes the page on every interface for the duration of a login.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_AUTH_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Fixed port for the browser-login page, so a container can publish it (e.g. 43117). Optional; a positive integer, and by default the page takes an ephemeral port.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_AUTH_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Seconds to wait for a browser login before the call fails with an error naming the remedies. Optional; a positive integer no larger than 2147483, and any other value is ignored. Defaults to 900.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_AUTH_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to attempt the browser login even where the server detects it cannot present one (CI, a container, a remote shell with no display). Use it when the login page is reachable from a browser elsewhere.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_FORCE_BROWSER

environmentVariables.description: Seconds a Form.io request may go unanswered before the call fails with a network error naming the URL. Optional; a positive integer no larger than 2147483, and any other value is ignored. Defaults to 60. project_import and project_export wait 300 seconds, or this value when it is longer.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to skip TLS certificate verification only for requests to the configured deployment (the hosts of the resolved project URL and base URL); every other host is verified as usual. For local development against self-signed certificates only — never enable in production.
environmentVariables.name: FORMIO_INSECURE_TLS

versionedDescriptions.description: The 0.1.11 package preserves the 28-tool stdio discovery contract. request_missing returns an id; get_request reads status. run_local is stdio-only when HUGGING_BAY_MCP_ENABLE_RUN_LOCAL=1.

environmentVariables.description: Ed25519 public key (base64url) that MCP_AUTH_MODE=signed-key verifies license tokens against. environmentVariables.description: When set, a license token must carry exactly this audience or it is rejected — a declarative scope check on top of the key, so a token minted for another deployment fails even if it verifies. WARNING: enabling this lets an AI model provision, modify and delete billable resources in a live IONOS CLOUD account. environmentVariables.description: API key for HTTP authentication. Required to bind the HTTP transport or the dashboard beyond loopback (0.0.0.0, a LAN address, a container): without it the server refuses to start

environmentVariables.description: Path to a file whose trimmed contents are the API key (the secret-file pattern Docker and Kubernetes mount). Set this or IRIS_API_KEY, not both; further keys and rotation are security.apiKeys in config.json
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_API_KEY_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to run a non-loopback bind with NO API key on purpose (lifts the startup refusal; the network is then your boundary)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED

environmentVariables.description: SQLite database path
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DB_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Which SQLite driver holds the database: native (better-sqlite3, the default) or node (Node's built-in node:sqlite, Node 22.13+). Unset: native, falling back to node when the native module cannot load
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_SQLITE_DRIVER

environmentVariables.description: How long one trace search may read before it answers with the matches found so far, in milliseconds (50-60000, default 1000)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_SEARCH_BUDGET_MS

environmentVariables.description: on (default) or off. off keeps no full-text index of the traces: writes are cheaper, and a search reads the traces within its time budget
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_SEARCH_INDEX

environmentVariables.description: Log level: debug, info, warn, error
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Directory for the database, custom rules and preferences (default ~/.iris)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_HOME

environmentVariables.description: Enables evaluate_with_llm_judge and verify_citations with an Anthropic model. Optional: the deterministic rules never need a key
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Enables evaluate_with_llm_judge and verify_citations with an OpenAI model. Optional: the deterministic rules never need a key
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OPENAI_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Hard cap on the worst-case cost of one LLM judge call (default 0.25); max_cost_usd can lower it for a call, never raise it
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_MAX_COST_USD_PER_EVAL

environmentVariables.description: A priced judge model; answers_the_ask then asks it on every evaluation with input, sending that input and output to the model's provider, and gates on its verdict (off by default)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: What every judge call together may spend per UTC day, per tenant, in USD (default 1): the relevance judge, evaluate_with_llm_judge and verify_citations. Past it no judge call is made
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD

environmentVariables.description: The name of IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD before 0.21.0. Read when the new name is unset, and it then limits every judge call
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD

environmentVariables.description: Relevance judge calls one request may make (default 20)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_MAX_CALLS_PER_REQUEST

environmentVariables.description: on (default) replaces the PII and credentials no_pii flags before the relevance judge sends input and output to its provider; off sends them as they are
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_REDACT

environmentVariables.description: Let verify_citations fetch URLs (off by default); a tool argument can turn it off for a call, never on
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_ALLOW_FETCH

environmentVariables.description: Start the dashboard alongside the server (same as --dashboard)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD

environmentVariables.description: Dashboard port (default 6920); IRIS_PORT is the MCP HTTP transport port (default 3000)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD_PORT

environmentVariables.description: MCP HTTP transport port (default 3000); only used with --transport http
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_PORT

environmentVariables.description: OTLP/HTTP collector URL; when set, every stored trace is also exported as OpenTelemetry spans (best-effort, asynchronous)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OTEL_ENDPOINT

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated domain allowlist for verify_citations fetches (only consulted when IRIS_CITATION_ALLOW_FETCH is on); a tool argument can narrow it, never add to it
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_DOMAINS

environmentVariables.description: The most one verify_citations call may spend on judge calls, in USD (default 1); max_cost_usd_total can lower it, never raise it
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_MAX_COST_USD_TOTAL

environmentVariables.description: Transport: stdio (default) or http; same as --transport
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_TRANSPORT

environmentVariables.description: Bind host for the HTTP transport (default 127.0.0.1); only used with --transport http
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated Origin allowlist for the HTTP transport and dashboard CORS (default http://localhost:*)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

environmentVariables.description: The most array elements and object keys one input may hold before it is validated (default 100000): a tool call's arguments, and a dashboard or OTLP JSON request body. A tool call over it gets an error result; a body, 413. OTLP protobuf has its own ceiling, one element per 5 bytes of the request size limit
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_MAX_INPUT_ELEMENTS

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_MAX_TOOL_INPUT_ELEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Bind host for the dashboard (default 127.0.0.1); same as --dashboard-host

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated key=value headers sent with every OTLP export (for example an auth token for your collector)

environmentVariables.description: service.name resource attribute on exported spans (default iris-eval)

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated packages whose write tools are not registered at all; the read tools of those packages stay available.

headers.description: Bearer <token>. The endpoint runs in OAuth mode: a client that speaks the OAuth flow needs no header at all and discovers the authorization server from the 401 challenge. A GitLab personal access token also works here, sent as 'Bearer glpat-...', which keeps clients with no OAuth flow working. It travels per request and is never stored server-side.
headers.name: Authorization

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription: KinToolkit connects AI agents to public US medicine label references. Five tools find bottles by bounded public brand, ingredient and bottle-audience filters; list five calculator-supported bottles and 20 published label rows; and retrieve exact printed label directions with plain-English explanations. Two tools also discover and read every published question guide, returning full website Markdown with all tables, formulation distinctions, sources, update dates and safety boundaries. Guide-only chewables and Claritin remain outside the calculator bottle catalog. Calculator bottles are Children's and Infants' Tylenol (acetaminophen), Children's and Infants' Motrin (ibuprofen), and Children's Zyrtec (cetirizine). A separate library contains nine exact CVS, Equate and Walgreens formulations with flavor, package NDC, label revision and DailyMed source. Those entries are reference-only, not calculator-supported substitutes. Label lookups preserve printed mL amounts or ask-doctor outcomes, age and weight bands, full directions, frequency and maximum limits, source and reference URL. Educational reference for adult caregivers: no personalized dosing, patient measurements, diagnosis, prescribing or concentration conversion. No sign-in or API key required.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.overview:
Find your next B2B customers. Know why they fit.

Describe the companies you want to reach. Leadbase researches matching businesses and relevant decision-makers, then saves the results with sources in an editable sheet. Start with 200 free credits in a new workspace and test your own target market.

Qualify companies by the criteria that matter to your offer: services, region and publicly evidenced business signals. Research DACH SMEs and German craft businesses alongside other target markets.

Turn existing accounts into a more useful prospect list. Enrich selected rows or entire columns, research relevant professional contacts and check available contact details. Review the evidence behind returned information before choosing your next step.

Keep control of the result. Follow progress, edit your sheet, filter the list and export the data. Continue the same research instead of rebuilding the list each time.

Use Leadbase with ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other compatible MCP clients. Connect your workspace and ask for a small list in your own target market. Research uses workspace credits.

server.description: Local log forensics: compress logs into citable evidence with root-cause confidence tiers.
server.title: log-ai-compressor

benchmark.note: Measured on 10 Loghub-2.0 datasets (ISSTA'24) whose event templates are human-annotated. At an equal 32k-token budget, evidence retention vs Drain3 is 7 wins / 1 tie / 2 losses - the two losses (HPC, Mac) are documented with root causes rather than hidden. Output size stays bounded in the low hundreds of tokens regardless of log size (re-measured 313-788 tokens on 120k-180k line logs), whereas Drain3's output grows from 317 to 566,802 tokens. Full methodology and limitations: https://github.com/hu-chenyu/log-ai-compressor/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md

privacy.note: All analysis runs on-device. The server only reads local file paths the calling agent passes in; no network calls are made unless the optional AI-interpretation layer is explicitly configured.

tools.description: Analyze one or more local log files (merged oldest-first by mtime, suitable for rotated logs). Returns error clusters ranked by priority, each with a root-cause confidence tier (CONFIRMED / LIKELY / INSUFFICIENT) and an explicit list of what evidence is still missing. Runs fully on-device.
tools.name: analyze_log_file

tools.description: Analyze a log text directly — pasted content, command output, or a fragment an agent already read. Same clustering and root-cause confidence output, without touching the filesystem.
tools.name: analyze_log_text

tools.description: Compare 2-5 log files and list errors that are new, disappeared, or common relative to a baseline file. Answers 'what changed between this deploy and the last one'.
tools.name: compare_log_files

tools.description: Export analysis as a compressed report in md / json / text / html / summary format. Markdown and summary are tuned for pasting into an LLM: a few hundred tokens instead of millions of raw log lines, with every finding still carrying its line numbers for citation.
tools.name: export_report

tools.description: Retrieve the full evidence for one error cluster: representative raw log line, surrounding context lines, de-noised stack trace, instance line-number index, and the reasoning behind its root-cause verdict.
tools.name: get_cluster_detail

tools.description: List built-in log parsing rule templates and the log formats each targets. Check this first when a log parses badly.
tools.name: list_rules

tools.description: Re-read the source log and re-verify every evidence reference in a report: file, line range, sha256 digest. Returns one of four verdicts - VERIFIED (every reference matches), TAMPERED (content really changed), UNVERIFIABLE (cannot check right now, e.g. the log is momentarily locked by another process - NOT an accusation of tampering), NO_EVIDENCE. This is the tool's trust anchor - the agent does not need to believe the analysis, it can re-run this step itself.
tools.name: verify_evidence

tools.description: Self-check with no arguments: confirms the tool is importable and reports version, available built-in rules, and whether optional AI interpretation is configured.
tools.name: check_environment

environmentVariables.description: Bare fallback for MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_BASE_URL (embeddings). For the summarize tool it only routes traffic when an API key already enables the feature; it never enables summarize by itself.

environmentVariables.description: Bare fallback for MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL.
environmentVariables.name: OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Maximum seconds an index-backed tool or resource waits for the FTS index to become queryable during a cold-start background build before raising IndexUnavailableError(reason="timeout"). Increase for large vaults.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S

environmentVariables.description: Maximum seconds an index-querying read tool waits for the IndexWriter to drain when called with wait_for_pending_writes=true. On timeout the tool answers from the current index and reports index_stale=true in the response _meta.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S

environmentVariables.description: Path to the markdown vault directory. When it does not exist, or the server cannot access it, the server starts but every tool fails with a message saying which until it is fixed (managed git mode clones into it). Symbolic links inside the vault are followed on Python 3.13+.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Set to true to hide the write tools (write, edit, append, delete, rename, move_folder, fetch, git_sync, the okf_* tools, create_upload_link) and serve a search-only vault.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_READ_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Refuse a write that would overwrite an existing file when no if_match etag is supplied. Deliberate replacement still works: read the file first, then pass if_match. Unaffected: edit, append, delete, rename. Set to false to allow blind overwrites.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_WRITE_PROTECT_EXISTING

environmentVariables.description: Set to true to have write, edit and append list, under unresolved_links, the target of each link the call added that get_broken_links reports. Links the note already held are left out. Off by default, leaving those responses unchanged.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_REPORT_UNRESOLVED_LINKS

environmentVariables.description: Hide the MCP Apps UI tools (browse_vault, show_context) from the tool listing for clients that do not render MCP Apps panels.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DISABLE_APPS_UI

environmentVariables.description: Path to the SQLite FTS5 index file; unset keeps the index in memory. Set it for persistence across restarts.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INDEX_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Path to the change-tracking state file. Defaults to INDEX_PATH plus .state.json (index.db.state.json beside index.db); without INDEX_PATH the state is kept in memory. Never written into the vault by default.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_STATE_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Base path for the embeddings files. Defaults beside INDEX_PATH (index-db-embeddings.npy and .json beside index.db); without INDEX_PATH the vectors are kept in memory and rebuilt at each start. Setting it also lets the provider be auto-detected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDINGS_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields promoted to the tag index for structured filtering. Changing it cold-rebuilds the index once on next startup; SEARCHABLE_FIELDS inherits this value when unset.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INDEXED_FIELDS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields required on every document; documents missing any are excluded from the index.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_REQUIRED_FIELDS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated glob patterns excluded from scanning, e.g. .obsidian/**,.trash/**.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EXCLUDE

environmentVariables.description: Frontmatter field used as the document title (falls back to title, the first H1, then the filename). Changing it cold-rebuilds the index once on next startup.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TITLE_FIELD

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields whose text values become keyword-searchable and enrich first-chunk embeddings. Inherits INDEXED_FIELDS when unset; the sentinel none means filterable but not searchable. Changing it cold-rebuilds the index and re-embeds once on next startup.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SEARCHABLE_FIELDS

environmentVariables.description: Relative folder where note templates live (used by the create_from_template prompt).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TEMPLATES_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Directory of .md prompt files that extend or override built-in prompts; a relative path is resolved against SOURCE_DIR.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_PROMPTS_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Filename of the per-folder conventions files surfaced to clients at write time (bare .md filename without glob characters). Set to none to disable folder conventions.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CONVENTIONS_FILE

environmentVariables.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) read semantics. With auto (the default), read annotations switch on when the vault declares an OKF version in its root index.md. Use off to disable OKF semantics entirely, or on to force them for an undeclared vault. Annotations are read-only; write behavior is never affected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_MODE

environmentVariables.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) enforced write layer. When true on an OKF-active vault, the server stamps generated provenance on each write and clears any verified attestation when a note's content changes. It also keeps each written folder's log.md and index.md current, and exposes the okf_verify tool. Requires OKF_MODE to be auto or on (a true value with OKF_MODE=off is a config error). Off by default.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_WRITE

environmentVariables.description: How the okf_verify tool attributes a human review. This applies only when OKF_WRITE is on, which gates the tool. With elicit (the default), okf_verify asks the human to confirm the review through an MCP elicitation, then records the attestation only on an affirmative reply. It fails closed when the client cannot elicit or the human declines, so a model holding the human's token cannot self-attest. Set trust-auth instead to attribute to a token's sub claim with no confirmation; it rejects static bearer credentials and other client-ID-only identities. This is safe only when the sole caller is a human-driven UI. Set off to hide the tool, leaving attestation to external tooling. A non-default value with OKF_WRITE off is a config error.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_VERIFY

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowed attachment extensions (e.g. pdf,png,jpg); case and a leading dot are ignored, so PDF and .pdf name the same type. Use * to allow every non-markdown file. Unset selects the built-in allowlist. A link whose target has a listed extension is not part of the link graph; changing the list rebuilds the index once.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_ATTACHMENT_EXTENSIONS

environmentVariables.description: Maximum attachment size in MB returned by read / accepted by write; 0 disables the limit.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Maximum bytes returned by a full-document read of a note; use `read(path, section=…)` for partial reads. 0 disables the limit.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_NOTE_READ_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Mode used when a search call omits 'mode': auto, keyword, semantic, or hybrid. The default 'auto' picks hybrid when embeddings are configured and keyword when they are not. Pin 'keyword' to keep unqualified searches off the embedding provider (each hybrid or semantic search embeds the query, which costs an API call on a metered provider). A configured semantic/hybrid default also degrades to keyword without embeddings, so no setting can make a vault unsearchable; an explicit mode= argument is never downgraded.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DEFAULT_SEARCH_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Maximum chunks returned per document in search results.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CHUNKS_PER_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Width of the snippet window (words) in search results; 0 returns full chunk content.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SNIPPET_WORDS

environmentVariables.description: Down-weights longer chunks in ranking: score / (1 + alpha * log(chunk_count)).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LENGTH_DOWNWEIGHT_ALPHA

environmentVariables.description: Word cap per chunk; the adaptive chunker splits at deeper heading levels, then paragraph/word boundaries, to respect it. Match it to the embedding model's context. A reindex applies a new value.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_CHUNK_WORDS

environmentVariables.description: Character cap enforced alongside MAX_CHUNK_WORDS to bound token-dense chunks. Unset derives min(1500, model context * 2.8). Set a positive value for an exact cap, or -1 to scale with the model's full context (can exhaust memory on long-context models). A reindex applies a new value.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS

environmentVariables.description: Words of overlap between adjacent budget-split fragments of the same heading section (0 disables). A reindex applies a new value.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CHUNK_OVERLAP_WORDS

environmentVariables.description: Folder-prefix score multipliers (`prefix:weight` pairs, comma-separated, weights > 0) applied to all search modes; the deepest matching prefix wins (sessions:0.5 demotes sessions/**).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FOLDER_WEIGHTS

environmentVariables.description: Per-column BM25 weights (`column:weight` pairs, comma-separated, weights >= 0) for keyword ranking. Columns: path, title, folder, heading, content, summary.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FTS_WEIGHTS

environmentVariables.description: Embedding provider: openai, voyage, ollama, or fastembed; setting it turns on search by meaning. environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: OpenAI-compatible API base URL for embeddings; the bare OPENAI_BASE_URL is honoured as a fallback.

environmentVariables.description: OpenAI-compatible embedding model name; the bare OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL is honoured as a fallback.

environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FASTEMBED_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Enrich embedding input with the note title, chunk heading, and (first chunk) searchable-field values. Flipping it re-embeds the whole vault once on next startup.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBED_CONTEXT

environmentVariables.description: Token/password for HTTPS git auth; remotes must be HTTPS when set.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: HTTPS remote URL for managed git mode: the server clones into an empty SOURCE_DIR on startup (or validates an existing origin) and enables the pull loop, auto-commit, and deferred push.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_REPO_URL

environmentVariables.description: Username for HTTPS git auth prompts (x-access-token for GitHub, oauth2 for GitLab, the account name for Bitbucket).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: Seconds between git fetch + fast-forward update attempts; 0 disables periodic pull.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_PULL_INTERVAL_S

environmentVariables.description: Seconds of write-idle time before pushing; 0 pushes only on shutdown.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_PUSH_DELAY_S

environmentVariables.description: Git committer name for auto-commits, and the author name too unless an OIDC claim supplies one; set this in Docker where git config user.name is empty.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Git committer email for auto-commits, and the author email too unless an OIDC claim supplies one.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL

environmentVariables.description: OIDC claim key used as the commit author name (e.g. name) when an OIDC token is present; the committer stays GIT_COMMIT_NAME. The claim is resolved when the tool call arrives and carried to the background commit, so it applies on every write. A configured claim the token does not carry is reported once at WARNING and the static identity is used.

environmentVariables.description: OIDC claim key used as the commit author email (e.g. email) when an OIDC token is present; the committer stays GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL. Resolved and carried the same way as the name claim.

environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_LFS
