environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER

environmentVariables.description: Seconds of quiet after the last filesystem event before reindexing.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER_DEBOUNCE_S

environmentVariables.description: Keep the non-recursive watch on the vault root; set false to register zero source-dir-rooted FSEvents streams (avoids repeated macOS access prompts on a home-rooted vault) at the cost of root-level files relying on scans.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER_ROOT_FLOOR

environmentVariables.description: Reconcile offline changes at startup by reindexing once the initial build completes. Set false on a large vault to start without paying a full filesystem scan per server start; changes made while no server was running are then invisible until a reindex runs (the reindex tool, or 'markdown-vault-mcp reindex'). Note that `index_stale` reports writer idleness, not agreement with disk, so it reads false while the index may still differ from the vault.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BOOT_REINDEX

environmentVariables.description: Shared secret for the GitHub push-event webhook; when set, mounts POST /github-webhook on HTTP/SSE transports to trigger an immediate pull + reindex on push events.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: Signing token for the GitLab push-event webhook (GitLab 19.0+); when set, mounts POST /gitlab-webhook on HTTP/SSE transports to trigger an immediate pull + reindex on push events. GitLab generates this value; copy the `whsec_` token it shows under Generate signing token rather than inventing one. Deliveries are authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 over the webhook id, timestamp and body, and a delivery older than 5 minutes is rejected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Secret token for the GitLab push-event webhook, GitLab's plain-text form and the only one below 19.0; also mounts POST /gitlab-webhook. It proves nothing about the body and cannot expire, so prefer the signing token where the GitLab version offers it. Setting both accepts either, which is how an existing webhook migrates.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Crashed-handler reclaim window in seconds for an in-flight reservation.

environmentVariables.description: Expected `aud` claim; tokens issued for another audience are rejected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OIDC_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: Scopes a caller must present, space- or comma-separated. Defaults to `openid` in oidc-proxy mode.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OIDC_REQUIRED_SCOPES

environmentVariables.description: Scopes advertised to MCP clients in protected-resource metadata, space- or comma-separated. Overrides the default `openid offline_access`; `oidc_required_scopes` is always added on top. Set this when the registered client is not permitted `offline_access`, or to have clients request extra claim scopes (such as `groups`) without also requiring them in every token.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OIDC_ADVERTISED_SCOPES

environmentVariables.description: Signing key for issued tokens; used in oidc-proxy mode only. When unset, the key is derived deterministically from `oidc_client_secret`, so tokens survive a restart. Rotating that secret then invalidates every issued token. Set this explicitly to decouple token validity from secret rotation. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OIDC_JWT_SIGNING_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Validate the access token instead of the id token.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OIDC_VERIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Persistent-state backend URL shared by every pvl-core subsystem that needs state. `memory://` is in-process and lost on restart; `file:///path` persists on one server; `redis://`, `dynamodb://` and `mongodb://` each need their matching extra. When unset, defaults to `file:///data/state` (the volume family Docker images mount), or to `memory://` (with a warning) on a host where that directory is not usable.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_KV_STORE_URL

environmentVariables.description: MCP Apps iframe domain, used for CSP sandboxing. Overrides the host derived from `base_url`.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_APP_DOMAIN

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated explicit tool names this instance exposes; every other tool is hidden from listings and cannot be invoked. Names matching no registered tool are inert. Mutually exclusive with `tools_deny`. Takes effect through `apply_tool_visibility`.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TOOLS_ALLOW

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated explicit tool names hidden from this instance (absent from listings, cannot be invoked). Names matching no registered tool are inert. Mutually exclusive with `tools_allow`. Takes effect through `apply_tool_visibility`.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TOOLS_DENY

environmentVariables.description: Explicit auth-mode override, accepting `remote` or `oidc-proxy` (case- and whitespace-insensitive). When unset the mode is auto-detected from which auth variables are set; the override exists because having all four OIDC variables set is ambiguous between those two modes. Other values are ignored with a warning.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_AUTH_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Path to a TOML file mapping bearer tokens to subjects; overrides the single-token `bearer_token` mode.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BEARER_TOKENS_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Subject assigned to the single-token bearer mode; ignored when `bearer_tokens_file` is set, since mapped mode carries per-token subjects.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BEARER_DEFAULT_SUBJECT

environmentVariables.description: Rename this server instance; defaults to the project name.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SERVER_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Concise routing context that distinguishes this deployment's material or responsibility.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION

environmentVariables.description: Deployment-specific behavioral policy added to the generated MCP instructions.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA

environmentVariables.description: Legacy: replaces all generated MCP instructions (deprecated; use _INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION for routing and _INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA for policy).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS

environmentVariables.description: Mount path for the MCP endpoint; the health routes derive their prefix from it.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_HTTP_PATH

environmentVariables.description: How much the unauthenticated /health and /health/ready bodies say: status, standard (adds name, version and per-check verdicts), or full (adds redacted reasons; trusted networks only).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_HEALTH_DETAIL

environmentVariables.description: Run the server process as this UID; the container entrypoint reassigns ownership of writable paths to match.
environmentVariables.name: PUID

environmentVariables.description: Run the server process as this GID; pair with PUID to match the owner of a mounted volume.
environmentVariables.name: PGID

environmentVariables.description: Log level for every logger in the process, FastMCP's included (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL). The -v CLI flag overrides to DEBUG. The unprefixed FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL still works for one major version and logs a deprecation warning.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Log rendering. rich is one colour event key=value line per record, for a terminal; json is one JSON object per record, for a collector. Unset picks rich when stderr is a terminal and json everywhere else, so a container or journald gets JSON with no configuration.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_FORMAT

environmentVariables.description: Ollama server URL for the ollama embedding provider. Bare (not MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_-prefixed), matching the Ollama ecosystem convention.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_HOST

environmentVariables.description: OpenAI API key for the openai embedding provider, and the fallback key for the summarize tool when MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_API_KEY is unset. Bare (not MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_-prefixed), matching the OpenAI ecosystem convention.
environmentVariables.name: OPENAI_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Voyage AI API key for the voyage embedding provider. Bare (not MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_-prefixed), matching the OPENAI_API_KEY / OLLAMA_HOST convention. Setting it never auto-selects the provider; choose it explicitly with MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=voyage.
environmentVariables.name: VOYAGE_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Bare fallback for MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_BASE_URL (embeddings). For the summarize tool it only routes traffic when an API key already enables the feature; it never enables summarize by itself.
environmentVariables.name: OPENAI_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Bare fallback for MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL.
environmentVariables.name: OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Maximum seconds an index-backed tool or resource waits for the FTS index to become queryable during a cold-start background build before raising IndexUnavailableError(reason="timeout"). Increase for large vaults.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S

environmentVariables.description: Maximum seconds an index-querying read tool waits for the IndexWriter to drain when called with wait_for_pending_writes=true. On timeout the tool answers from the current index and reports index_stale=true in the response _meta.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S

environmentVariables.description: Path to the markdown vault directory. When it does not exist, or the server cannot access it, the server starts but every tool fails with a message saying which until it is fixed (managed git mode clones into it). Symbolic links inside the vault are followed on Python 3.13+.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Set to true to hide the write tools (write, edit, append, delete, rename, move_folder, fetch, git_sync, the okf_* tools, create_upload_link) and serve a search-only vault.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_READ_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Refuse a write that would overwrite an existing file when no if_match etag is supplied. Deliberate replacement still works: read the file first, then pass if_match. Unaffected: edit, append, delete, rename. Set to false to allow blind overwrites.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_WRITE_PROTECT_EXISTING

environmentVariables.description: Set to true to have write, edit and append list, under unresolved_links, the target of each link the call added that get_broken_links reports. Links the note already held are left out. Off by default, leaving those responses unchanged.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_REPORT_UNRESOLVED_LINKS

environmentVariables.description: Hide the MCP Apps UI tools (browse_vault, show_context) from the tool listing for clients that do not render MCP Apps panels.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DISABLE_APPS_UI

environmentVariables.description: Path to the SQLite FTS5 index file; unset keeps the index in memory. Set it for persistence across restarts.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INDEX_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Path to the change-tracking state file. Defaults to INDEX_PATH plus .state.json (index.db.state.json beside index.db); without INDEX_PATH the state is kept in memory. Never written into the vault by default.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_STATE_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Base path for the embeddings files. Defaults beside INDEX_PATH (index-db-embeddings.npy and .json beside index.db); without INDEX_PATH the vectors are kept in memory and rebuilt at each start. Setting it also lets the provider be auto-detected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDINGS_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields promoted to the tag index for structured filtering. Changing it cold-rebuilds the index once on next startup; SEARCHABLE_FIELDS inherits this value when unset.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INDEXED_FIELDS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields required on every document; documents missing any are excluded from the index.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_REQUIRED_FIELDS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated glob patterns excluded from scanning, e.g. .obsidian/**,.trash/**.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EXCLUDE

environmentVariables.description: Frontmatter field used as the document title (falls back to title, the first H1, then the filename). Changing it cold-rebuilds the index once on next startup.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TITLE_FIELD

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated frontmatter fields whose text values become keyword-searchable and enrich first-chunk embeddings. Inherits INDEXED_FIELDS when unset; the sentinel none means filterable but not searchable. Changing it cold-rebuilds the index and re-embeds once on next startup.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SEARCHABLE_FIELDS

environmentVariables.description: Relative folder where note templates live (used by the create_from_template prompt).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TEMPLATES_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Directory of .md prompt files that extend or override built-in prompts; a relative path is resolved against SOURCE_DIR.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_PROMPTS_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Filename of the per-folder conventions files surfaced to clients at write time (bare .md filename without glob characters). Set to none to disable folder conventions.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CONVENTIONS_FILE

environmentVariables.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) read semantics. With auto (the default), read annotations switch on when the vault declares an OKF version in its root index.md. Use off to disable OKF semantics entirely, or on to force them for an undeclared vault. Annotations are read-only; write behavior is never affected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_MODE

environmentVariables.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) enforced write layer. When true on an OKF-active vault, the server stamps generated provenance on each write and clears any verified attestation when a note's content changes. It also keeps each written folder's log.md and index.md current, and exposes the okf_verify tool. Requires OKF_MODE to be auto or on (a true value with OKF_MODE=off is a config error). Off by default.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_WRITE

environmentVariables.description: How the okf_verify tool attributes a human review. This applies only when OKF_WRITE is on, which gates the tool. With elicit (the default), okf_verify asks the human to confirm the review through an MCP elicitation, then records the attestation only on an affirmative reply. It fails closed when the client cannot elicit or the human declines, so a model holding the human's token cannot self-attest. Set trust-auth instead to attribute to a token's sub claim with no confirmation; it rejects static bearer credentials and other client-ID-only identities. This is safe only when the sole caller is a human-driven UI. Set off to hide the tool, leaving attestation to external tooling. A non-default value with OKF_WRITE off is a config error.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_VERIFY

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowed attachment extensions (e.g. pdf,png,jpg); case and a leading dot are ignored, so PDF and .pdf name the same type. Use * to allow every non-markdown file. Unset selects the built-in allowlist. A link whose target has a listed extension is not part of the link graph; changing the list rebuilds the index once.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_ATTACHMENT_EXTENSIONS

environmentVariables.description: Maximum attachment size in MB returned by read / accepted by write; 0 disables the limit.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Maximum bytes returned by a full-document read of a note; use `read(path, section=…)` for partial reads. 0 disables the limit.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_NOTE_READ_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Mode used when a search call omits 'mode': auto, keyword, semantic, or hybrid. The default 'auto' picks hybrid when embeddings are configured and keyword when they are not. Pin 'keyword' to keep unqualified searches off the embedding provider (each hybrid or semantic search embeds the query, which costs an API call on a metered provider). A configured semantic/hybrid default also degrades to keyword without embeddings, so no setting can make a vault unsearchable; an explicit mode= argument is never downgraded.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_DEFAULT_SEARCH_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Maximum chunks returned per document in search results.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CHUNKS_PER_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Width of the snippet window (words) in search results; 0 returns full chunk content.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SNIPPET_WORDS

environmentVariables.description: Down-weights longer chunks in ranking: score / (1 + alpha * log(chunk_count)).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LENGTH_DOWNWEIGHT_ALPHA

environmentVariables.description: Word cap per chunk; the adaptive chunker splits at deeper heading levels, then paragraph/word boundaries, to respect it. Match it to the embedding model's context. A reindex applies a new value.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_CHUNK_WORDS

environmentVariables.description: Character cap enforced alongside MAX_CHUNK_WORDS to bound token-dense chunks. Unset derives min(1500, model context * 2.8). Set a positive value for an exact cap, or -1 to scale with the model's full context (can exhaust memory on long-context models). A reindex applies a new value.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS

environmentVariables.description: Words of overlap between adjacent budget-split fragments of the same heading section (0 disables). A reindex applies a new value.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_CHUNK_OVERLAP_WORDS

environmentVariables.description: Folder-prefix score multipliers (`prefix:weight` pairs, comma-separated, weights > 0) applied to all search modes; the deepest matching prefix wins (sessions:0.5 demotes sessions/**).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FOLDER_WEIGHTS

environmentVariables.description: Per-column BM25 weights (`column:weight` pairs, comma-separated, weights >= 0) for keyword ranking. Columns: path, title, folder, heading, content, summary.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FTS_WEIGHTS

environmentVariables.description: Embedding provider: openai, voyage, ollama, or fastembed; setting it turns on search by meaning. Unset auto-detects from the environment (never voyage), but only when EMBEDDINGS_PATH is set. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works with openai plus OPENAI_BASE_URL; see the embeddings guide.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER

environmentVariables.description: Ollama embedding model name.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OLLAMA_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Force Ollama to embed on CPU only.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OLLAMA_CPU_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Voyage AI embedding model name.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: OpenAI-compatible API base URL for embeddings; the bare OPENAI_BASE_URL is honoured as a fallback.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: OpenAI-compatible embedding model name; the bare OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL is honoured as a fallback.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: FastEmbed model name.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FASTEMBED_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: FastEmbed model cache directory (in Docker, stored under /data/state/fastembed).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Enrich embedding input with the note title, chunk heading, and (first chunk) searchable-field values. Flipping it re-embeds the whole vault once on next startup.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBED_CONTEXT

environmentVariables.description: Per-request wall-clock budget in seconds for a single embedding HTTP call (OpenAI/Ollama). The local FastEmbed backend runs in-process with no network call and ignores this. CPU-only or large-model workloads may need 60-120 s; raise this if batches time out.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S

environmentVariables.description: Number of chunks sent per embedding request. Smaller batches shorten each request (useful under a tight timeout on slow models) at the cost of more round-trips.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE

environmentVariables.description: Token/password for HTTPS git auth; remotes must be HTTPS when set.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: HTTPS remote URL for managed git mode: the server clones into an empty SOURCE_DIR on startup (or validates an existing origin) and enables the pull loop, auto-commit, and deferred push.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_REPO_URL

environmentVariables.description: Username for HTTPS git auth prompts (x-access-token for GitHub, oauth2 for GitLab, the account name for Bitbucket).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: Seconds between git fetch + fast-forward update attempts; 0 disables periodic pull.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_PULL_INTERVAL_S

environmentVariables.description: Seconds of write-idle time before pushing; 0 pushes only on shutdown.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_PUSH_DELAY_S

environmentVariables.description: Git committer name for auto-commits, and the author name too unless an OIDC claim supplies one; set this in Docker where git config user.name is empty.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Git committer email for auto-commits, and the author email too unless an OIDC claim supplies one.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL

environmentVariables.description: OIDC claim key used as the commit author name (e.g. name) when an OIDC token is present; the committer stays GIT_COMMIT_NAME. The claim is resolved when the tool call arrives and carried to the background commit, so it applies on every write. A configured claim the token does not carry is reported once at WARNING and the static identity is used.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_NAME_CLAIM

environmentVariables.description: OIDC claim key used as the commit author email (e.g. email) when an OIDC token is present; the committer stays GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL. Resolved and carried the same way as the name claim.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL_CLAIM

environmentVariables.description: Run git lfs pull on startup to fetch LFS-tracked attachments; set to false for repos without LFS.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_LFS

environmentVariables.description: Watch the vault for external filesystem changes; auto-disabled when git pull is active or a webhook can deliver (HTTP/SSE transports only). Requires the file-watcher extra.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER

environmentVariables.description: Seconds of quiet after the last filesystem event before reindexing.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER_DEBOUNCE_S

environmentVariables.description: Keep the non-recursive watch on the vault root; set false to register zero source-dir-rooted FSEvents streams (avoids repeated macOS access prompts on a home-rooted vault) at the cost of root-level files relying on scans.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_FILE_WATCHER_ROOT_FLOOR

environmentVariables.description: Reconcile offline changes at startup by reindexing once the initial build completes. Set false on a large vault to start without paying a full filesystem scan per server start; changes made while no server was running are then invisible until a reindex runs (the reindex tool, or 'markdown-vault-mcp reindex'). Note that `index_stale` reports writer idleness, not agreement with disk, so it reads false while the index may still differ from the vault.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BOOT_REINDEX

environmentVariables.description: Shared secret for the GitHub push-event webhook; when set, mounts POST /github-webhook on HTTP/SSE transports to trigger an immediate pull + reindex on push events.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: Signing token for the GitLab push-event webhook (GitLab 19.0+); when set, mounts POST /gitlab-webhook on HTTP/SSE transports to trigger an immediate pull + reindex on push events. GitLab generates this value; copy the `whsec_` token it shows under Generate signing token rather than inventing one. Deliveries are authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 over the webhook id, timestamp and body, and a delivery older than 5 minutes is rejected.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Secret token for the GitLab push-event webhook, GitLab's plain-text form and the only one below 19.0; also mounts POST /gitlab-webhook. It proves nothing about the body and cannot expire, so prefer the signing token where the GitLab version offers it. Setting both accepts either, which is how an existing webhook migrates.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Summarization backend (only openai is recognised). Unset auto-detects: the backend activates when credentials or an explicit endpoint are present.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_PROVIDER

environmentVariables.description: API key for the OpenAI-compatible summarize endpoint; the bare OPENAI_API_KEY is honoured as a fallback. Unset works for keyless local endpoints (Ollama).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint base URL for the summarize tool; setting it enables the tool even without an API key. The bare OPENAI_BASE_URL routes traffic only when a key already enables the feature.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Chat model id used for summaries.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_OPENAI_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Upper bound on generated tokens per summarize call; on reasoning models this budget also covers internal reasoning tokens.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_MAX_TOKENS

environmentVariables.description: Cap on the number of notes summarised in one call (subtree expansion truncates to this many).
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_MAX_NOTES

environmentVariables.description: Aggregate cap on note characters sent to the model in one call; excess is truncated with a flag on the result.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_MAX_INPUT_CHARS

environmentVariables.description: Per-request wall-clock budget in seconds for a single summarize backend call; keep it below the MCP client's request timeout so the server-side error wins the race.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Link lifetime in seconds when the caller requests no explicit TTL.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_TTL_DEFAULT_S

environmentVariables.description: Ceiling in seconds a caller-requested link TTL is clamped to.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_TTL_MAX_S

environmentVariables.description: Post-success grace window in seconds: a served token's TTL shrinks to this so a stalled transfer can retry within it.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_GRACE_TTL_S

environmentVariables.description: Crashed-handler reclaim window in seconds for an in-flight reservation.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_LEASE_S

environmentVariables.description: Maximum size in bytes of a single upload.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_TRANSFER_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Seconds a long-running tool call may run in the foreground before it is promoted to a background job and a job handle is returned instead.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_JOBS_SOFT_DEADLINE_S

environmentVariables.description: Seconds a background-job record (working or finished) is retained for polling before it expires from the store.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_JOBS_RESULT_TTL_S

environmentVariables.description: Maximum live background jobs per calling subject; further promotions are rejected until older records expire.
environmentVariables.name: MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_JOBS_MAX_PER_SUBJECT

packageArguments.description: Named destination: service-keys/<name>.json and sessions/<name>.env under AUTH_BROKER_PATH or the platform directory, read field by field. The working directory's .env is not loaded.
packageArguments.name: --mcp

environmentVariables.description: Path to the .env file that states the destination (the same as the --env-path argument). The file states SAP_URL and SAP_AUTH_TYPE (basic, snc or jwt); a jwt file also states SAP_GRANT_TYPE (authorization_code or none). Without this or --mcp, the server starts in tool-inspection-only mode: nothing is read from the working directory, and SAP_* variables in the process environment alone form no destination.

environmentVariables.description: Base directory of service-keys/ and sessions/ for a named destination chosen with the --mcp argument (one directory; a list is not split). Default: ~/.config/mcp-abap-adt (Documents\mcp-abap-adt on Windows).

environmentVariables.description: Browser for a JWT login: chrome, edge, firefox, system, headless or none.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_BROWSER

environmentVariables.description: Callback port of the JWT browser login, 1-65535.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_BROWSER_AUTH_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Write a named destination's session to disk (sessions/<name>.env) instead of keeping it in memory.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_UNSAFE

environmentVariables.description: Connection type: http or rfc. SNC needs rfc (and the SAP NW RFC SDK).
environmentVariables.name: SAP_CONNECTION_TYPE

environmentVariables.description: System type, required (here or as --system-type; no default, never guessed): the tools offered (e.g. Programs are onprem-only), the connector, and how the system's answers are read. Without it a destination does not start.
environmentVariables.name: SAP_SYSTEM_TYPE

environmentVariables.description: Logon language (ISO code, e.g. 'en', 'de').
environmentVariables.name: SAP_LANGUAGE

environmentVariables.description: System context for on-prem create/update operations (system id).
environmentVariables.name: SAP_MASTER_SYSTEM

environmentVariables.description: Responsible user for on-prem create/update operations.

server.name: dev.workers.pathwren.www/mcp-endpoint-lint
server.description: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"whoami","arguments":{}}} free no key
server.title: MCP Endpoint Lint - handshake, tool schemas, JSON-RPC errors

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: none - no key, no account, no OAuth

example.note: whoami takes no arguments at all and answers about the request you just sent - user-agent, address, what our classifier makes of it. Every tool here accepts {} and answers with its own documented worked example, run against a built-in fixture: no outbound request is made and no third party is touched. Send the request below verbatim. To lint a real endpoint, pass your own url - this server fetches the URL you give it, and only that.

markdown.canonical: the HTML page; each mirror carries Link: rel="canonical" back to it
markdown.note: Everything this server answers from is also readable without JSON-RPC and without an MCP client: every page of the host is a plain markdown file at the same address with .md — also .mdx, <page>.html.md, <page>.html.mdx, or send Accept: text/markdown to the .html page. No key, no JavaScript, CC0. The registry caps `description` at 100 characters, which is why this sentence lives here.

outbound_requests.only_to: the URL supplied by the caller in the tool arguments
outbound_requests.rate_limited: per caller, per target host, and per edge location
outbound_requests.refuses: its own publisher, ephemeral tunnel and preview hostnames, IP literals, private names, URLs carrying credentials, non-HTTP schemes and unusual ports - before any socket is opened
outbound_requests.storage: none - a caller's URL is never written to a database, a log line or a metric
outbound_requests.zero_argument_calls: run against a built-in fixture and make no outbound request at all

Deploy to Cloudflare: hapi deploy --name mcp-registry --openapi https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml --url https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io

server.description: Strava MCP tools for AI: athletes, activities, segments, clubs, routes. Powered by HAPI MCP server.
server.title: HAPI Strava MCP Server

examples.config: Add 'https://strava.run.mcp.com.ai/mcp' as a remote MCP server in your MCP client, then sign in to Strava when prompted.
examples.description: Connect once and let your MCP client + HAPI handle OAuth2 Authorization Code flow and token exchange.
examples.name: Basic Connection

examples.description: This server exposes Strava operations as MCP tools for athlete, activities, segments, clubs, routes, uploads, and streams.
examples.name: What You Can Do
examples.note: Example tools include getLoggedInAthlete, getLoggedInAthleteActivities, getSegmentById, getClubById, createUpload, and getActivityStreams.

examples.config: hapi deploy --name strava --project strava --openapi https://docs.mcp.com.ai/apis/openapi/strava.json --url https://www.strava.com/api/v3 --host https://strava.run.mcp.com.ai
examples.description: Publish your Strava MCP Server with a public host your clients can reach.
examples.name: Deploy your own in One Command

notes: MCP clients must support OAuth2 Authorization Code flow for Strava integrations.
HAPI handles the heavy lifting for OAuth2 flow and API tool exposure.
Default Strava API base URL: https://www.strava.com/api/v3.
The --host value is required because ChatGPT, Claude, and other MCP clients connect to your server using that external FQDN/URL. Used to generate the absolute URLs as per MCP specification.
Use a public internet hostname (or VPN-reachable internal FQDN/IP) that clients can access.
OAuth endpoints: https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize and https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token.
OpenAPI source: https://docs.mcp.com.ai/apis/openapi/strava.json
Documentation: https://docs.mcp.com.ai/deployment/

server.description: Detect the employee programs a company publishes: ERGs, DEI, benefits, leave, volunteering.

server.name: ai.moxt/mcp-workspace
server.description: Browse and manage files in your Moxt AI workspace from any MCP client.
server.title: Moxt Workspace

headers.description: Bearer token. Use your Moxt API Key (moxt_...) from https://moxt.ai/settings/tokens
headers.name: Authorization

server.name: io.github.groove79/mcp-world-calendar
server.description: Public holidays and working-day math for 200+ countries and regions, local weekends. No keys.
server.title: World Business Calendar

server.name: io.github.codespar/mcp-worldpay
server.description: MCP server for Access Worldpay — enterprise processor: authorize, capture, refund, tokenize

environmentVariables.description: Access Worldpay API username (Basic Auth)
environmentVariables.name: WORLDPAY_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: Access Worldpay API password (Basic Auth)
environmentVariables.name: WORLDPAY_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Merchant entity identifier assigned during onboarding. Injected as merchant.entity into every request body.
environmentVariables.name: WORLDPAY_ENTITY

environmentVariables.description: sandbox | production. Defaults to sandbox. sandbox -> https://try.access.worldpay.com, production -> https://access.worldpay.com.
environmentVariables.name: WORLDPAY_ENV

environmentVariables.description: Payments API version for the Content-Type/Accept media-type header. Defaults to v7.
environmentVariables.name: WORLDPAY_API_VERSION

server.name: io.github.goran-revops/mcp-write-gate
server.description: Sits in front of any MCP server. Reads pass, writes are checked against your lists.
server.title: MCP Write Gate

packageArguments.description: The name the real server was given with mcp-write-gate add
Path to gate.json, if it is not in the default gate folder
packageArguments.name: --config

server.name: io.github.hannasdev/mcp-writing
server.description: Metadata-first fiction editing and reasoning tools for long-form writing projects.
server.title: Writing MCP

environmentVariables.description: Path to the manuscript sync folder that mcp-writing indexes and edits.
environmentVariables.name: WRITING_SYNC_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Optional path for the SQLite index database used by the server.
environmentVariables.name: DB_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Startup ownership policy for sync-folder files.
environmentVariables.name: OWNERSHIP_GUARD_MODE

Required in self-hosted mode (MCP_DEPLOYMENT_MODE unset or self-hosted) unless MICETRO_API_KEY is used instead — the server needs exactly one of the two credential options. environmentVariables.name: MICETRO_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Micetro API key (Micetro 26.1 and later). Alternative to MICETRO_USERNAME + MICETRO_PASSWORD; wins over the username/password pair when both are set. Every outbound request carries `authorization: Bearer <key>` and no session login is performed. Unlike MICETRO_USERNAME/MICETRO_PASSWORD, which are simply not used in horizon mode, MICETRO_API_KEY is rejected at startup there — cloud mode has no fixed backend identity for a key to authenticate.
environmentVariables.name: MICETRO_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Client authentication mode for the /mcp endpoint. One of: none | static-key | signed-key | resource-server. Required at runtime — the server refuses to start without it (no default).

environmentVariables.name: MCP_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Ed25519 public key (base64url) that MCP_AUTH_MODE=signed-key verifies license tokens against. DEFAULTS TO A SHARED DEMO KEY, which authenticates a token holder rather than a customer — every BlueCat-issued token for this server verifies against it. For anything beyond a trial, generate a per-deployment key pair (license-keygen --gen-key) and set this to its public half.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ED25519_PUBLIC_KEY

environmentVariables.description: When set, a license token must carry exactly this audience or it is rejected — a declarative scope check on top of the key, so a token minted for another deployment fails even if it verifies. Unset means the aud claim is not checked. Only meaningful with MCP_AUTH_MODE=signed-key.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_SIGNED_KEY_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: Token issuer URL, matched against the iss claim of incoming JWTs. Required when MCP_AUTH_MODE=resource-server — the server refuses to start in that mode without it.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER

environmentVariables.description: JWKS endpoint whose public keys verify the signature on every incoming Bearer JWT. Required when MCP_AUTH_MODE=resource-server — the server refuses to start in that mode without it.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_JWKS_URI

environmentVariables.description: Expected JWT aud claim for MCP_AUTH_MODE=resource-server. A token carrying a different audience, or no aud claim at all, is rejected. Unset skips audience validation entirely.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_OAUTH_AUDIENCE

packageArguments.description: When set to true, allows configuration values to be overridden via request headers and query parameters.
packageArguments.name: --allowRequestOverrides

packageArguments.description: Atlas API client ID for authentication. Required for running Atlas tools.
packageArguments.name: --apiClientId

packageArguments.description: Atlas API client secret for authentication. Required for running Atlas tools.
packageArguments.name: --apiClientSecret

packageArguments.description: Base URL for the MongoDB Assistant API.
packageArguments.name: --assistantBaseUrl

packageArguments.description: Time in milliseconds that temporary database users created when connecting to MongoDB Atlas clusters will remain active before being automatically deleted.
packageArguments.name: --atlasTemporaryDatabaseUserLifetimeMs

packageArguments.description: Comma separated values of tool names that require user confirmation before execution. Requires the client to support elicitation.
packageArguments.name: --confirmationRequiredTools

packageArguments.description: Visibility scope for MongoDB connections created at runtime. With 'session' (the default), each MCP session only sees the connections it created (plus the shared 'preconfigured' one) and they are closed when the session ends — recommended when the HTTP transport is exposed to multiple clients without authentication. With 'global', connections are shared across all sessions and survive session rotation.
packageArguments.name: --connectionScope

packageArguments.description: MongoDB connection string for direct database connections. Optional, if not set, you'll need to call the connect tool before interacting with MongoDB data.
packageArguments.name: --connectionString

packageArguments.description: When set to true, disallows the use of server-side JavaScript operators (such as $where, $function, and $accumulator) in query filters and aggregation pipelines.
packageArguments.name: --disableServerSideJs

packageArguments.description: Comma separated values of tool names, operation types, and/or categories of tools that will be disabled.
packageArguments.name: --disabledTools

packageArguments.description: When true, runs the server in dry mode: dumps configuration and enabled tools, then exits without starting the server.
packageArguments.name: --dryRun

packageArguments.description: Time in milliseconds the user has to respond to an elicitation request (such as a tool confirmation prompt) before it fails.
packageArguments.name: --elicitationTimeoutMs

packageArguments.description: Time in milliseconds between export cleanup cycles that remove expired export files.
packageArguments.name: --exportCleanupIntervalMs

packageArguments.description: Time in milliseconds after which an export is considered expired and eligible for cleanup.
packageArguments.name: --exportTimeoutMs

packageArguments.description: Folder to store exported data files.
packageArguments.name: --exportsPath

packageArguments.description: When true, the HTTP transport allows requests with a session ID supplied externally through the 'mcp-session-id' header. When an external ID is supplied, the initialization request is optional.
packageArguments.name: --externallyManagedSessions

packageArguments.description: Deprecated. Use `monitoringServerHost` instead. Host address to bind the healthCheck HTTP server to (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `healthCheckPort` must also be set.
packageArguments.name: --healthCheckHost

packageArguments.description: Deprecated. Use `monitoringServerPort` instead. Port number for the healthCheck HTTP server (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `healthCheckHost` must also be set.
packageArguments.name: --healthCheckPort

packageArguments.description: Maximum size of the HTTP request body in bytes (only used when transport is 'http'). This value is passed as the optional limit parameter to the Express.js json() middleware.
packageArguments.name: --httpBodyLimit

packageArguments.description: Header that the HTTP server will validate when making requests (only used when transport is 'http').
packageArguments.name: --httpHeaders

packageArguments.description: Host address to bind the HTTP server to (only used when transport is 'http').
packageArguments.name: --httpHost

packageArguments.description: Port number for the HTTP server (only used when transport is 'http'). Use 0 for a random port.
packageArguments.name: --httpPort

packageArguments.description: The HTTP response type for tool responses: 'sse' for Server-Sent Events, 'json' for standard JSON responses.
packageArguments.name: --httpResponseType

packageArguments.description: Idle timeout for a client to disconnect (only applies to http transport).
packageArguments.name: --idleTimeoutMs

packageArguments.description: When set to true, enforces that query operations must use an index, rejecting queries that perform a collection scan.
packageArguments.name: --indexCheck

packageArguments.description: Folder to store logs.
packageArguments.name: --logPath

packageArguments.description: Comma separated values of logger types.
packageArguments.name: --loggers

packageArguments.description: Maximum number of MongoDB connections a single scope (an MCP session by default, see connectionScope) can hold open. When exceeded, the scope's least-recently-used connection is closed and its connectionId revoked. The preconfigured connection does not count towards the limit.
packageArguments.name: --maxActiveConnections

packageArguments.description: The maximum size in bytes for results from a find or aggregate tool call. This serves as an upper bound for the responseBytesLimit parameter in those tools.
packageArguments.name: --maxBytesPerQuery

packageArguments.description: The maximum number of documents that can be returned by a find or aggregate tool call. For the find tool, the effective limit will be the smaller of this value and the tool's limit parameter.
packageArguments.name: --maxDocumentsPerQuery

packageArguments.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions the HTTP transport will hold in memory (only used when transport is 'http'). Each session holds a full server instance, transport, and timers, so choose a value based on your deployment's available memory; the default is a conservative safety net rather than a recommended production value.
packageArguments.name: --maxSessions

packageArguments.description: The maximum time in milliseconds that operations are allowed to run on the MongoDB server. When set, this value is passed as the maxTimeMS option to read operations such as find, aggregate, and count.
packageArguments.name: --maxTimeMS

packageArguments.description: Minimum severity level for log messages forwarded to the MCP client.
packageArguments.name: --mcpClientLogLevel

packageArguments.description: Features to expose on the monitoring server (only used when transport is 'http' and monitoringServerHost/monitoringServerPort are set).
packageArguments.name: --monitoringServerFeatures

packageArguments.description: Host address to bind the monitoring HTTP server to (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `monitoringServerPort` must also be set.
packageArguments.name: --monitoringServerHost

packageArguments.description: Port number for the monitoring HTTP server (only used when transport is 'http'). If provided, `monitoringServerHost` must also be set.
packageArguments.name: --monitoringServerPort

packageArguments.description: Notification timeout for a client to be aware of disconnect (only applies to http transport).
packageArguments.name: --notificationTimeoutMs

packageArguments.description: Comma separated values of preview features that are enabled.
packageArguments.name: --previewFeatures

packageArguments.description: When set to true, only allows read, connect, and metadata operation types, disabling create/update/delete operations.
packageArguments.name: --readOnly

packageArguments.description: When set to disabled, disables telemetry collection.
packageArguments.name: --telemetry

packageArguments.description: Either 'stdio' or 'http'.
packageArguments.name: --transport

packageArguments.description: API key for Voyage AI embeddings service (required for creating Atlas Local deployments with auto-embed vector search capabilities).
packageArguments.name: --voyageApiKey

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to close the shared "global" namespace on this server. Every call that routes there is refused before the request is sent, and the tools stop offering it as an example. Unset leaves it available. A value that is neither a yes nor a no stops the server rather than being read as no.

environmentVariables.description: An OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint you run. Set it and embeddings are computed on this machine rather than by Noetive: a publish carries the vector alongside its text, and a query's anchor phrases are replaced by vectors so they are never sent. This is not confidential publishing: message text still travels, because that is what a search returns. The endpoint must answer to the same model name as NOETIVE_MODEL and return NOETIVE_DIMENSIONS values. Plain http is accepted only for a loopback address. Inside a container 127.0.0.1 is the container itself; use host.docker.internal.

environmentVariables.description: Preset name: english (default, bge-small-en-v1.5), english-fast, english-quality, multilingual, multilingual-quality, multilingual-ollama. Ignored when EMBEDDING_MODEL is set.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_PRESET

environmentVariables.description: Power-user override: any transformers.js checkpoint or Ollama model id. Takes precedence over EMBEDDING_PRESET. Switching auto-reindexes.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Embedding backend. 'transformers' (local, default) or 'ollama' (requires a running Ollama server).
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER

environmentVariables.description: Base URL of a local Ollama server. Only used when EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Override the embedding dimensionality when EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama. If unset, the server probes the model on startup.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_DIM

environmentVariables.description: Override Ollama's num_ctx for embed requests. Leave UNSET to let obsidian-brain auto-detect via `/api/show`'s `context_length` (e.g. nomic-embed-text=2048, bge-m3=8192, qwen3-embedding:0.6b=32 768). Setting this manually imposes a hard cap and may silently truncate longer inputs — see https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14259. Ollama's own default is 2048 which truncates for any model trained on a larger context. See also https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/7008. Fallback when both env is unset AND /api/show is unreachable: 8192.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_NUM_CTX

environmentVariables.description: Auto-pull the configured Ollama model when /api/show returns 404 (model not present). Default ON — choosing an Ollama-backed preset is implicit consent to download its model. Streams /api/pull progress to stderr. Set to '0' to disable auto-pull entirely (master kill-switch) and fall back to the actionable error path (`HTTP 404 — try: ollama pull <model>`).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_AUTO_PULL

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in to auto-pull for BYOM (custom EMBEDDING_MODEL) Ollama models OUTSIDE Ollama's official `library/` namespace. Default OFF — third-party models (e.g. `user/custom-fork`, `myregistry.com/team/model`) require this env var to be set to `1` before they will auto-pull, to prevent silent downloads of arbitrary user-named artifacts. Preset-known models (via EMBEDDING_PRESET) and bare model ids in the official library (e.g. `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`, `library/llama3:8b`) continue to auto-pull by default per the existing OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_AUTO_PULL behavior.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_BYOM_AUTO_PULL

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to disable the live chokidar file watcher. Useful on SMB/NFS vaults where FSEvents/inotify don't fire reliably — fall back to running `obsidian-brain index` on a schedule (launchd/systemd).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_WATCH

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to skip the startup catchup reindex pass that picks up edits made while the server was down. The live file watcher still starts (via OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_WATCH=1 to disable that separately), and first-time indexing on an empty DB is unaffected — this knob only governs the post-restart `enqueueBackgroundReindex` walk.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_CATCHUP

environmentVariables.description: Per-file reindex debounce for the live watcher, in milliseconds.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Graph-wide community-detection (Louvain) debounce for the live watcher, in milliseconds. Louvain is the only expensive op — batching it prevents per-edit CPU spikes.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_COMMUNITY_DEBOUNCE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Per-tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Tools exceeding this return an MCP error instead of hanging.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Override the adaptive chunk-size budget (in tokens). When set, this beats the capacity probed from the model's tokenizer or Ollama /api/show. Use for debugging or for models with stale tokenizer configs.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS

environmentVariables.description: Override the per-user config directory where obsidian-brain stores model overrides (`model-overrides.json`) and the user-fetched seed (`seed-models.json`). Default is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian-brain` on macOS/Linux (or `~/.config/obsidian-brain`) and `%APPDATA%/obsidian-brain` on Windows. Both files survive `npm update obsidian-brain` because they live outside the package.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_CONFIG_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Set to "1" to print a verbose synchronous startup trace to stderr — every preflight, createContext, server.connect, and shutdown step is logged with a monotonic timestamp. The LAST line before any silent failure tells you exactly which step the server reached. No-op when unset (no overhead). Use to diagnose silent-crash failure modes.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_DEBUG

environmentVariables.description: Default "true". Set "false" to forbid any tool from marking a message read on OurFamilyWizard - reading a body for the first time stamps a co-parent-visible "First Viewed" time that cannot be undone. A ceiling: no per-call argument can raise it.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_ALLOW_MARK_READ

environmentVariables.description: Default "false". Whether ofw_sync_messages fetches unread inbox bodies by default (each fetch stamps a First Viewed time). Capped by OFW_ALLOW_MARK_READ.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_FETCH_UNREAD_BODIES

environmentVariables.description: Allow list of days message content may be read, e.g. "mon,thu" (weekdays, YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD, in DISPLAY_TZ). Other days: subjects only, nothing marked read. Unset = every day.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_READ_DAYS

environmentVariables.description: Deny list of days message content may NOT be read (same format as OFW_READ_DAYS; wins over it). Unset = none.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_NO_READ_DAYS

environmentVariables.description: Set to false to disable the on-disk session cache and re-authenticate on every process start. Defaults to enabled.

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path for the session cache file. Defaults to $MCP_DATA_DIR/.ofw-mcp/session.json.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_SESSION_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Set true to register only healthcheck plus expense tools. All profile/dashboard, message, calendar, and journal tools are structurally absent.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_EXPENSE_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Set true for strict reimbursement upload mode: only healthcheck, ofw_upload_expense_pdf, ofw_create_expense, and ofw_update_expense register. Excludes ofw_mark_expense_reimbursed. Implies OFW_EXPENSE_ONLY.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_EXPENSE_UPLOAD_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Set "true" to return attachments as MCP content blocks by default (images render directly; other files come back as embedded resources) instead of writing to disk. Callers can still override per call via the tool's `inline` argument.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_INLINE_ATTACHMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Where ofw_download_attachment writes (default ~/Downloads/ofw-mcp). Every disk write is confined to it: a saveTo outside it (after resolving symlinks) is refused, and an existing file is replaced only with force:true.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_ATTACHMENTS_DIR

environmentVariables.description: The only directory ofw_upload_attachment may read from (default: OFW_ATTACHMENTS_DIR). Paths outside it after resolving symlinks, hidden files/dirs, and files over 25 MiB are refused.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_UPLOAD_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Explicit cache-key label; overrides OFW_USERNAME for fetchproxy-only multi-account setups. If you have multiple OFW accounts and want them to use separate caches, set it to a label per profile.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_CACHE_IDENTITY

environmentVariables.description: Overrides the message cache directory (default ~/.cache/ofw-mcp).
environmentVariables.name: OFW_CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Skip the fetchproxy fallback, so missing credentials become a hard error (useful in headless CI).
environmentVariables.name: OFW_DISABLE_FETCHPROXY

environmentVariables.description: When a cached read comes back EMPTY from a non-fresh cache, the read tools sync the backing folders and answer from the refreshed cache instead of refusing with UNVERIFIED_EMPTY (default off, i.e. refuse). Per-call autoRefresh overrides it. A refresh that does not make the read verifiable still refuses.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_AUTO_REFRESH

environmentVariables.description: How long a verified-against-OFW folder stays labelled `fresh` in read tools' `freshness` block (default 300). Unusable values fall back to the default — a typo must never widen the window in which stale data reads as current.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS

environmentVariables.description: Per-call OFW-request budget for ofw_sync_messages: a positive integer caps how many OFW requests one sync call may make before pausing; the next call resumes where it left off. Unset means unbounded (local installs walk fully in one call).
environmentVariables.name: OFW_SYNC_MAX_REQUESTS

environmentVariables.description: Per-request timeout for OFW API calls, in milliseconds (default 30000). Each retry gets its own fresh window.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Log every OFW request/response to stderr (Authorization redacted). Diagnostic only.
environmentVariables.name: OFW_DEBUG_LOG

environmentVariables.description: IANA zone (e.g. America/New_York, the default) for every `<field>Display` value, and the zone a NAIVE source timestamp is assumed to be wall-clock in. OFW's API reports naive local times in the account's own zone, so this must match it. Unrecognized values fall back to the default.
environmentVariables.name: DISPLAY_TZ

environmentVariables.description: Localhost port of the fetchproxy concentrator the ContextMint Bridge extension connects to (default 37149). Every MCP on one machine shares it, so move it for all of them or not at all.

environmentVariables.description: Bind interface for the fetchproxy concentrator, a literal IP only (default 127.0.0.1). Keep on loopback; it exists for hosted deployments that run each MCP in its own network namespace.

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path where the fetchproxy long-term identity keypair is stored (default ~/.fetchproxy/identity/).

environmentVariables.name: OSM_OVERPASS_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated ordered list of Overpass endpoints. A failure advances to the next entry within the same tool call; a single entry means no failover. An entry written url|N gets N slots of its own and adds capacity, for an instance whose operator allows parallel queries, never a public FOSSGIS server; an unsuffixed later entry is failover only. Write a | inside a URL as %7C. Verify a mirror's usage policy, data coverage, and freshness before adding it. Ignored when OSM_OVERPASS_BASE_URL is set.
environmentVariables.name: OSM_OVERPASS_ENDPOINTS

environmentVariables.description: Concurrent Overpass queries per endpoint: OSM_OVERPASS_BASE_URL, and every OSM_OVERPASS_ENDPOINTS entry not sized with |N. With no |N entry it is also the most queries in flight across all endpoints. A query waits at most 30 seconds in total for a slot, then fails with pacer_shed and a retryAfter. The default of 1 follows the public FOSSGIS instances, which allow one query in flight per user; raise it only for an instance whose operator allows parallel queries, such as a private or paid one.

server.name: io.github.aoreshkov/oracle-forms-mcp
server.description: Serves Oracle Forms module content (.fmb/.mmb/.pll/.olb) from a directory to MCP clients.
server.title: Oracle Forms

packageArguments.description: Directory containing the Oracle Forms modules (in copy-mode, the pre-converted *_fmb.xml/*.pld files live here). Mount it into the container and point --forms-dir at the mount.
packageArguments.name: --forms-dir

packageArguments.description: Optional. Directory the converted XML / .pld text forms are written into — the converter runs with this as its working directory, one flat directory for all modules, each file named after its module (orders_fmb.xml, utils.pld). Mount a writable volume and point this at it to keep the text forms outside the cache. Must not be the forms directory. Also settable as OFMCP_CONVERTED_DIR.
packageArguments.name: --converted-dir

packageArguments.description: Optional. Site-supplied converter run instead of Oracle's frmf2xml: a whole command line with its arguments, quoting any part that contains spaces, or a JSON array of arguments. It is spawned directly, never through a shell; the module's path replaces {} and is appended when {} is absent, the output file's path replaces {out}, and the working directory is the converted directory (--converted-dir, else the module's cache directory), which is where it must write the text form unless it writes to {out}. Mount the converter into the container and point this at it. Also settable as OFMCP_CONVERT_COMMAND.
packageArguments.name: --convert-command

packageArguments.description: Optional. Converter for .pll libraries only, run instead of whatever would convert them otherwise; same syntax and placeholders as --convert-command. frmcmp writes its .pld next to the module unless told otherwise, so give it Output_File={out}. Also settable as OFMCP_COMPILE_COMMAND.
packageArguments.placeholder: /opt/forms/frmcmp.sh Module={} Module_Type=LIBRARY Script=YES Batch=YES Logon=NO Output_File={out}
packageArguments.name: --compile-command

environmentVariables.description: Same as --converted-dir, for clients that set environment variables rather than arguments. The flag wins when both are given.
environmentVariables.name: OFMCP_CONVERTED_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Same as --convert-command — the whole command line, not just an executable — for clients that set environment variables rather than arguments. The flag wins when both are given.
environmentVariables.name: OFMCP_CONVERT_COMMAND

environmentVariables.description: Same as --compile-command — the whole command line for converting .pll libraries — for clients that set environment variables rather than arguments. The flag wins when both are given.
environmentVariables.name: OFMCP_COMPILE_COMMAND

runtimeRequirements.liveConversion: Converting binary .fmb/.pll in place needs an Oracle Forms installation (ORACLE_HOME) on the host; Oracle's frmf2xml/frmcmp tools are proprietary and are never bundled.
runtimeRequirements.mcpb: A JRE 25+: the Java installation chosen in the bundle's settings, else JAVA_HOME, else the java on PATH. MCPB manifests can only declare Node/Python runtimes, so this cannot be expressed in the bundle itself.
runtimeRequirements.oci: None — the image is self-contained, but it is copy-mode only: it serves modules that have already been converted to text (*_fmb.xml / *.pld) next to the modules in the mounted directory.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.account_required: A free Pantry Butler account. No approval process, no waitlist.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.auth: OAuth 2.1. Clients register themselves (RFC 7591 dynamic client registration) and authorize with PKCE S256 — no token to paste and no key to issue by hand. Discovery is the standard one: an unauthenticated call to /mcp returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer to https://thepantrybutler.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Scopes are read and write; write implies read. Long-lived bearer tokens from https://thepantrybutler.com/connect still work for scripts and self-hosted clients.

Overrides the default `openid offline_access`; `oidc_required_scopes` is always added on top. Set this when the registered client is not permitted `offline_access`, or to have clients request extra claim scopes (such as `groups`) without also requiring them in every token.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_OIDC_ADVERTISED_SCOPES

environmentVariables.description: Signing key for issued tokens; used in oidc-proxy mode only. When unset, the key is derived deterministically from `oidc_client_secret`, so tokens survive a restart. Rotating that secret then invalidates every issued token. Set this explicitly to decouple token validity from secret rotation. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_OIDC_JWT_SIGNING_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Validate the access token instead of the id token.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_OIDC_VERIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Persistent-state backend URL shared by every pvl-core subsystem that needs state. `memory://` is in-process and lost on restart; `file:///path` persists on one server; `redis://`, `dynamodb://` and `mongodb://` each need their matching extra. When unset, defaults to `file:///data/state` (the volume family Docker images mount), or to `memory://` (with a warning) on a host where that directory is not usable.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_KV_STORE_URL

environmentVariables.description: MCP Apps iframe domain, used for CSP sandboxing. Overrides the host derived from `base_url`.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_APP_DOMAIN

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated explicit tool names this instance exposes; every other tool is hidden from listings and cannot be invoked. Names matching no registered tool are inert. Mutually exclusive with `tools_deny`. Takes effect through `apply_tool_visibility`.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_TOOLS_ALLOW

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated explicit tool names hidden from this instance (absent from listings, cannot be invoked). Names matching no registered tool are inert. Mutually exclusive with `tools_allow`. Takes effect through `apply_tool_visibility`.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_TOOLS_DENY

environmentVariables.description: Explicit auth-mode override, accepting `remote` or `oidc-proxy` (case- and whitespace-insensitive). When unset the mode is auto-detected from which auth variables are set; the override exists because having all four OIDC variables set is ambiguous between those two modes. Other values are ignored with a warning.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_AUTH_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Path to a TOML file mapping bearer tokens to subjects; overrides the single-token `bearer_token` mode.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_BEARER_TOKENS_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Subject assigned to the single-token bearer mode; ignored when `bearer_tokens_file` is set, since mapped mode carries per-token subjects.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_BEARER_DEFAULT_SUBJECT

environmentVariables.description: Rename this server instance; defaults to the project name.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_SERVER_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Concise routing context that distinguishes this deployment's material or responsibility.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION

environmentVariables.description: Deployment-specific behavioral policy added to the generated MCP instructions.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA

environmentVariables.description: Legacy: replaces all generated MCP instructions (deprecated; use _INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION for routing and _INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA for policy).
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS

environmentVariables.description: Mount path for the MCP endpoint; the health routes derive their prefix from it.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_HTTP_PATH

environmentVariables.description: How much the unauthenticated /health and /health/ready bodies say: status, standard (adds name, version and per-check verdicts), or full (adds redacted reasons; trusted networks only).
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_HEALTH_DETAIL

environmentVariables.description: Run the server process as this UID; the container entrypoint reassigns ownership of writable paths to match.

environmentVariables.description: Run the server process as this GID; pair with PUID to match the owner of a mounted volume.
environmentVariables.name: PGID

environmentVariables.description: Log level for every logger in the process, FastMCP's included (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL). The -v CLI flag overrides to DEBUG. The unprefixed FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL still works for one major version and logs a deprecation warning.
environmentVariables.name: PAPERLESS_MCP_LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Log rendering. rich is one colour event key=value line per record, for a terminal; json is one JSON object per record, for a collector. Unset picks rich when stderr is a terminal and json everywhere else, so a container or journald gets JSON with no configuration.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.executionRule: V1 tools never authorize payment. Strict live verification creates only RESERVED. New accounts must CONSUME with exact provider binding in a credential-isolated gateway; older accounts retain legacy compatibility. A fresh claim authorizes an idempotent provider request, not exactly-once delivery. Reports and webhooks are hints. MandateShield checks configured Stripe or x402 evidence without trusting the caller before finalization. Caller-independent is not an external audit or independent-organization verification. Unknown or conflicting outcomes fail closed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.publicProofSemantics: Externally bound self-report; not users, installations, certification, or independently executed conformance.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.pricing: $0.01 per credit. 1 credit = 1 lens on 1 photo. Lookups and cache hits cost zero. New accounts get 1,000 free credits on email verification.
tools: analyze_photo: run AI vision lenses (dating, people, location, condition, atmosphere, automobile, and more) against one image; returns flat JSON keyed by field name.
analyze_batch: analyze 1 to 200 independent photos in one call; registry-first internally, surfaces creditsSaved.
list_lenses: free runtime discovery of every lens and stack with the output fields each owns.
lookup_photo: free registry check (URL, local path, sha256, or pHash) returning cached lens results without re-running the model.
get_credits: free balance read; reports the single spendable total.
purchase_credits: returns a wallet deep-link (checkout opens in the browser, never inside the MCP).
enrich_photo: write cached lens output into a file's EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata so the analysis travels with the photo (5 credits).

brand.disambiguation: Pinsvit is a single-word brand, spelled P-I-N-S-V-I-T, for a platform where people find and book local businesses and businesses run their bookings with Pinsvit Business. It is a distinct brand and is not affiliated with other, similarly spelled names.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.summary: Pinsvit helps people find and book local businesses — their services, prices and free times — in the app or through AI agents, alongside nearby events and posts. Pinsvit Business is the booking and management software those businesses run on, with a free tier available. It gives a business a public page, a service catalog, online booking, a front desk, a customer directory and per-booking billing, ready for AI agents. MCP covers the customer side (place lookup, services, bookable times, booking, cancelling and notes) and the front desk of a business (its bookings, booking requests, accepting and declining, no-shows, booking for a walk-in customer, reading a bill and recording a payment), plus public local discovery and content creation; setting a business up (its services, hours, settings, bill charges and discounts) is in the GraphQL API and the app.

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path of the one sandbox directory: path inputs are read from it and outputMode='file' outputs are written under it (never overwritten; the real path of every file read and of every parent written must stay inside — a planted symlink or junction is SECURITY_VIOLATION). Key-bearing files (.key .p8 .p12 .pfx) are read by the key tools only, never written, never served as resources. Unset: every tool works on inline PEM / base64 only.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in content-addressed response cache directory (SHA-256 keyed, 1h TTL, 256 MiB LRU, plaintext at rest). Never caches path inputs, file output, a call carrying a password or a signer, a clock-dependent instant, a random serial or nonce, describe_engine or draft_governance_issue.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Serve Streamable HTTP on this loopback port (POST /mcp) instead of stdio (MCP 2026-07-28, stateless, legacy fallback). Unauthenticated unless PKINATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN is set.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in bearer token for the HTTP transport (>= 16 chars, no whitespace; a weaker value refuses to start). When set, /mcp requires 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' or answers 401. Compared constant-time, never logged.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Operator-side password of the encrypted PKCS#8 key or PKCS#12 file the tools open (keeps the secret out of the model transcript). Exclusive with the per-call password input (both at once is VALIDATION_ERROR). Never logged; only its presence is reported at startup.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Pinned instant (ISO 8601 or epoch milliseconds) every omitted at / notBefore / signingTime falls back to, for reproducible verdicts and artefacts. Unset: the wall clock (a clock-dependent result is never cached). An invalid value refuses to start.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_AT

environmentVariables.description: Operator ceiling for limits.maxInputBytes and the decoded size of one PKI object (default 67108864 = 64 MiB, the engine default). Integer >= 1024, read once at startup; an invalid value refuses to start. A per-call value above it is refused with LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_INPUT_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Operator ceiling for limits.maxKdfIterations and limits.maxPkcs12KdfIterations (default 10000000, the engine default): the CPU bound of a hostile PBES2 key or PKCS#12 file. Integer >= 1, read once at startup; an invalid value refuses to start.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_KDF_ITERATIONS

environmentVariables.description: Operator ceiling for limits.maxPathsExplored (default 1000, the engine default): the RFC 5280 section 6 path-building work bound. Integer >= 1, read once at startup; an invalid value refuses to start.
environmentVariables.name: PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_PATHS_EXPLORED

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.summary: Plexarm is the operating system for self-organised AI agent teams: a hosted MCP server that holds the goals, initiatives and action items your agents and people work toward, with priorities, owners, dates and dependencies. It does not run agents. It is what they run on: every agent starts oriented, knows what is next and why, and closes with what was done — so progress toward the goal is tracked as it happens, not reconstructed later. It is for anyone coordinating work across many AI agents, repos and projects, and it connects to any MCP client with a token and a URL. You need a Plexarm account and a token: create a free account at plexarm.com, create a token at plexarm.com/me, and run /plexarm:connect to store it and check the connection. To install in Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add natalabs/plexarm-plugin, then /plugin install plexarm@plexarm.
